comments.content:
# Project: Arij

## Project Specification

# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

## Epic to Implement

### Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor

## Contexte

Arij dispose déjà de deux modes autonomes, mais ce sont tous les deux des rafales one-shot :
- `lib/pipeline/` fait passer *un* ticket par build → review → auto-fix puis s'arrête.
- `lib/night/` fait *une* passe DAG sur un lot d'epics puis se termine.

Aucun ne surveille le board en continu. Le mode Full Auto est le chaînon manquant : un superviseur permanent, activé par projet, avec des budgets de concurrence indépendants pour la build et la review.

Une fois activé, Arij en continu :
- build tout ce qui est en `todo`, plus tout ce qui est en `in_progress` sans agent dessus (ticket revenu d'une review négative) ;
- review tout ce qui est en `review` ;
- merge un ticket dès que sa review est propre.

## Décisions validées avec l'utilisateur

| Question | Réponse |
|---|---|
| Périmètre des tickets | Tous les tickets — epics, bugs et user stories |
| Merge après une review propre | Oui, le mode auto merge |
| Portée d'activation | Par projet |
| Si build+review > budget scheduler | Avertir seulement — ne jamais le remonter silencieusement |

## Réutilisation (ne rien réécrire)

| Besoin | Existant | Chemin |
|---|---|---|
| Dispatch build/review programmatique | `createPipelineStageDriver(...).launchStage({stage})` — « réplique les closures des routes au byte près pour que le board ne puisse pas distinguer une étape de pipeline d'un dispatch humain ». Supporte `scope: 'epic' \| 'story'`. | `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:140` |
| Primitive de merge | `mergeWorktree(gitRepoPath, branchName, worktreePath)` → `{merged, commitHash, error}` | `lib/git/manager.ts` |
| Porte « la review est OK » | Les gardes `→ done` du moteur de workflow | `lib/workflow/engine.ts:49-97` |
| Transition validée + event + log | `applyTransition({... source:'merge'})` | `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts:47` |
| « Un agent est-il déjà sur ce ticket ? » | `getRunningSessionForTarget(target)` — compte `queued` + `running` | `lib/agents/concurrency.ts:94` |
| « Ce ticket attend-il un humain ? » | `isAwaitingReply(signal)` — pur, client-safe | `lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:30` |
| Budget de slots + file FIFO | `agentScheduler.submit(projectId, sessionId, launch)` | `lib/agents/scheduler.ts:124` |
| Patron de boucle permanente | Watchdog : singleton globalThis, `start()` idempotent, interval `unref()`, `sweep(now)` pur pour les tests | `lib/agents/watchdog.ts` |
| Patron de registre mémoire | `NightRunRegistry` — map active + ring récent, pas de table | `lib/night/registry.ts` |
| Convention constantes client-safe | clé + fn clé par projet + défaut + `parseX` renvoyant `null` pour tomber au niveau suivant | `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts` |
| Wiring au boot | `register()` dans `instrumentation.ts` (démarre déjà le watchdog) | `instrumentation.ts` |
| UI sélecteur agent + concurrence | `NightRunDialog` compose déjà `NamedAgentSelect` + `Input` de concurrence + `OptionRow` | `components/night/NightRunDialog.tsx` |

## La machine à états boucle déjà toute seule

Vérifié dans `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` :
- lancement build → epic `→ in_progress`, branche créée (`:585`)
- build réussie → epic `→ review` (`:745`)
- verdict de review négatif → epic `→ in_progress` (`:916`), sans agent dessus
- verdict positif → l'epic reste en `review`

Le superviseur ne fait que dispatcher ; c'est le driver qui déplace les tickets. Un ticket rejeté retombe en `in_progress` sans agent et est naturellement repris au sweep suivant.

## Granularité : « tous les tickets » face à une branche par epic

Git est la contrainte. Il y a un worktree et une branche par epic — la route de build story écrit `epics.branchName` et réutilise le worktree de l'epic, et `getRunningSessionForTarget` en scope story matche aussi les sessions de l'epic parent (`lib/agents/concurrency.ts:65-70`), donc deux stories du même epic ne peuvent jamais tourner en parallèle. Cette garde existe déjà ; le mode auto en hérite gratuitement.

Règle retenue :
- Build → scope story quand l'epic a des stories (une à la fois par epic, plein d'epics en parallèle) ; scope epic sinon. La route de build story promeut déjà l'epic en `review` quand toutes les stories sœurs sont review/done (`stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:303-330`).
- Review et merge → toujours au scope epic. La branche est l'unité d'intégration et `epic.branchName` est ce qui se merge. Reviewer chaque story *puis* l'epic doublerait le coût en tokens pour le même diff.

## Les quatre pièges à traiter

1. Re-review infinie. Une review qui passe laisse l'epic en `review`. Un balayage naïf le re-reviewerait sans fin. → Un epic en `review` n'est candidat que s'il n'a aucune session de review terminale plus récente que sa dernière session de code terminale. Délibérément temporel, pas basé sur le verdict : le verdict est une heuristique de sous-chaîne sur le markdown de l'agent (`epics/[epicId]/review/route.ts:337`), sans champ structuré.

2. Écraser une question d'agent. Un agent finissant en `asked_question` laisse le ticket maintenu en `in_progress` par `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` (`lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:42`) — indiscernable de « revient de review » pour un sélecteur naïf. → Exclure tout ticket où `isAwaitingReply(...)` est vrai ; il redevient éligible dès que l'utilisateur répond par un commentaire.

3. Merger quelque chose qui n'est pas réellement approuvé. « Review OK » n'existe comme booléen nulle part. → Ne pas en inventer un. `applyTransition(→ done, source:'merge')` refuse déjà tant que `hasCompletedReview` est faux *ou* que `hasOpenReviewComments` est vrai (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`). Le mode auto tente la transition et traite un refus comme « pas prêt, on passe ». Sa propre porte est *plus stricte* que celle du moteur, car la fraîcheur du piège 1 compense le fait que `hasCompletedReview` est laxiste (`lib/workflow/context.ts:32-51`). → Ne surtout pas réutiliser `POST .../approve` : il résout en masse tous les commentaires de review ouverts (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), écrasant exactement les findings bloquants qui doivent empêcher un merge auto.

4. Double comptage des budgets. Build (N) + review (M) vivent *au-dessus* du budget `agent_max_concurrent` par projet (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`, défaut 3). Si N+M le dépasse, le mode admet du travail qui s'empile dans la file FIFO — et comme `getRunningSessionForTarget` compte les `queued`, le board paraît occupé sans rien exécuter. → Admission control sur ses propres sessions en vol, et avertissement dans le dialog quand N+M dépasse le budget (décision utilisateur : avertir seulement).

## Plan d'implémentation

Aucune migration. Toute la config vit dans la table clé/valeur `settings` existante et chaque session dispatchée est une ligne `agent_sessions` ordinaire.

# Project: Arij

## Project Specification

# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

## Epic to Implement

### Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor

## Contexte

Arij dispose déjà de deux modes autonomes, mais ce sont tous les deux des rafales one-shot :
- `lib/pipeline/` fait passer *un* ticket par build → review → auto-fix puis s'arrête.
- `lib/night/` fait *une* passe DAG sur un lot d'epics puis se termine.

Aucun ne surveille le board en continu. Le mode Full Auto est le chaînon manquant : un superviseur permanent, activé par projet, avec des budgets de concurrence indépendants pour la build et la review.

Une fois activé, Arij en continu :
- build tout ce qui est en `todo`, plus tout ce qui est en `in_progress` sans agent dessus (ticket revenu d'une review négative) ;
- review tout ce qui est en `review` ;
- merge un ticket dès que sa review est propre.

## La machine à états boucle déjà toute seule

Vérifié dans `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` :
- lancement build → epic `→ in_progress`, branche créée (`:585`)
- build réussie → epic `→ review` (`:745`)
- verdict de review négatif → epic `→ in_progress` (`:916`), sans agent dessus
- verdict positif → l'epic reste en `review`

Le superviseur ne fait que dispatcher ; c'est le driver qui déplace les tickets. Un ticket rejeté retombe en `in_progress` sans agent et est naturellement repris au sweep suivant.

## Granularité : « tous les tickets » face à une branche par epic

Git est la contrainte. Il y a un worktree et une branche par epic — la route de build story écrit `epics.branchName` et réutilise le worktree de l'epic, et `getRunningSessionForTarget` en scope story matche aussi les sessions de l'epic parent (`lib/agents/concurrency.ts:65-70`), donc deux stories du même epic ne peuvent jamais tourner en parallèle. Cette garde existe déjà ; le mode auto en hérite gratuitement.

Règle retenue :
- Build → scope story quand l'epic a des stories (une à la fois par epic, plein d'epics en parallèle) ; scope epic sinon. La route de build story promeut déjà l'epic en `review` quand toutes les stories sœurs sont review/done (`stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:303-330`).
- Review et merge → toujours au scope epic. La branche est l'unité d'intégration et `epic.branchName` est ce qui se merge. Reviewer chaque story *puis* l'epic doublerait le coût en tokens pour le même diff.

## Les quatre pièges à traiter

1. Re-review infinie. Une review qui passe laisse l'epic en `review`. Un balayage naïf le re-reviewerait sans fin. → Un epic en `review` n'est candidat que s'il n'a aucune session de review terminale plus récente que sa dernière session de code terminale. Délibérément temporel, pas basé sur le verdict : le verdict est une heuristique de sous-chaîne sur le markdown de l'agent (`epics/[epicId]/review/route.ts:337`), sans champ structuré.

2. Écraser une question d'agent. Un agent finissant en `asked_question` laisse le ticket maintenu en `in_progress` par `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` (`lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:42`) — indiscernable de « revient de review » pour un sélecteur naïf. → Exclure tout ticket où `isAwaitingReply(...)` est vrai ; il redevient éligible dès que l'utilisateur répond par un commentaire.

3. Merger quelque chose qui n'est pas réellement approuvé. « Review OK » n'existe comme booléen nulle part. → Ne pas en inventer un. `applyTransition(→ done, source:'merge')` refuse déjà tant que `hasCompletedReview` est faux *ou* que `hasOpenReviewComments` est vrai (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`). Le mode auto tente la transition et traite un refus comme « pas prêt, on passe ». Sa propre porte est *plus stricte* que celle du moteur, car la fraîcheur du piège 1 compense le fait que `hasCompletedReview` est laxiste (`lib/workflow/context.ts:32-51`). → Ne surtout pas réutiliser `POST .../approve` : il résout en masse tous les commentaires de review ouverts (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), écrasant exactement les findings bloquants qui doivent empêcher un merge auto.

4. Double comptage des budgets. Build (N) + review (M) vivent *au-dessus* du budget `agent_max_concurrent` par projet (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`, défaut 3). Si N+M le dépasse, le mode admet du travail qui s'empile dans la file FIFO — et comme `getRunningSessionForTarget` compte les `queued`, le board paraît occupé sans rien exécuter. → Admission control sur ses propres sessions en vol, et avertissement dans le dialog quand N+M dépasse le budget (décision utilisateur : avertir seulement).

129:export async function PUT(
130:  request: NextRequest,
131:  { params }: { params: Promise<{ projectId: string }> }
132:) {
133:  const { projectId } = await params;
134:
135:  const found = getProjectOr404(projectId);
136:  if (isErrorResponse(found)) return found;
137:
138:  const body = await request.json().catch(() => null);
139:  if (!body || typeof body !== "object") {
140:    return NextResponse.json(
141:      { error: "Invalid payload. Send a JSON object of auto mode settings." },
142:      { status: 400 }
143:    );
144:  }
145:
146:  const payload = body as Record<string, unknown>;
147:
148:  // Every field is optional so the dialog can toggle the switch without
149:  // resending the whole form. Values go through the same parsers the resolver
150:  // uses, so a clamp applies at write time as well as read time.
151:  //
152:  // The whole payload is validated into `writes` BEFORE anything is
153:  // persisted. Validating as we went would let `{enabled: true,
154:  // buildConcurrency: "lots"}` arm the mode and then return 400 — the caller
155:  // would believe nothing happened while a supervisor started dispatching.
156:  const writes: Array<[string, unknown]> = [];
157:
158:  if ("enabled" in payload) {
159:    const enabled = parseAutoModeEnabled(payload.enabled);
160:    if (enabled === null) {
161:      return NextResponse.json(
162:        { error: "`enabled` must be a boolean." },
163:        { status: 400 }
164:      );
165:    }
166:    writes.push([autoModeEnabledSettingKey(projectId), enabled]);
167:  }
168:
169:  // A named-agent id is only useful if it still resolves to a row. Writing an
170:  // unknown or since-deleted id would have the status endpoint report an agent
171:  // that dispatch quietly ignores — the mode would run for hours with a
172:  // provider the user never chose. `null` stays valid: it means "use the
173:  // normal resolution chain".
174:  for (const field of ["buildAgent", "reviewAgent"] as const) {
175:    if (!(field in payload)) continue;
176:    const agentId = parseAutoModeAgent(payload[field]);
177:    if (agentId !== null && !namedAgentExists(agentId)) {
178:      return NextResponse.json(
179:        { error: `\`${field}\` is not a known named agent.` },
180:        { status: 400 }
181:      );
182:    }
183:    writes.push([
184:      field === "buildAgent"
185:        ? autoModeBuildAgentSettingKey(projectId)
186:        : autoModeReviewAgentSettingKey(projectId),
187:      agentId,
188:    ]);
189:  }
190:
191:  if ("buildConcurrency" in payload) {
192:    const value = parseAutoModeConcurrency(payload.buildConcurrency);
193:    if (value === null) {
194:      return NextResponse.json(
195:        { error: "`buildConcurrency` must be an integer between 0 and 10." },
196:        { status: 400 }
197:      );
198:    }
199:    writes.push([autoModeBuildConcurrencySettingKey(projectId), value]);
200:  }
201:
202:  if ("reviewConcurrency" in payload) {
203:    const value = parseAutoModeConcurrency(payload.reviewConcurrency);
204:    if (value === null) {
205:      return NextResponse.json(
206:        { error: "`reviewConcurrency` must be an integer between 0 and 10." },
207:        { status: 400 }
208:      );
209:    }
210:    writes.push([autoModeReviewConcurrencySettingKey(projectId), value]);
211:  }
212:
213:  try {
214:    // All-or-nothing: a half-applied configuration is how an unattended mode
215:    // ends up running with settings nobody chose.
216:    db.transaction(() => {
217:      for (const [key, value] of writes) putSetting(key, value);
218:    });
219:
220:    // Mirror the persisted flag into the registry BEFORE building the
221:    // response, so the runtime fields the dialog reads back (`running`, and
222:    // the in-flight counts a disable clears) describe the state the caller
223:    // just asked for rather than the one the sweep has not caught up with.
224:    const config = resolveAutoModeConfigForProject(projectId);
225:    autoModeRegistry.setEnabled(projectId, config.enabled);
226:
227:    const status = buildStatus(projectId);
228:
229:    // Enabling (or retuning) takes effect now, not on the next 15s tick.
230:    // Disabling also sweeps: that pass is what settles the registry state.
231:    kickAutoMode(projectId);
232:
233:    return NextResponse.json({ data: status });
234:  } catch (error) {
235:    return errorResponse(error, "Failed to update auto mode settings");
236:  }
237:}

### Summary of Delivered Work: Full Auto Mode

We have implemented **Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor** in full accordance with the epic specification and all user stories.

---

### Implementation Details by User Story

#### 1. Configuration & Constants (`lib/auto-mode/constants.ts`, `lib/auto-mode/config.ts`)
- Client-safe `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` importing nothing from `lib/db`, defining global settings keys and per-project key helpers (`autoModeEnabledSettingKey`, `autoModeBuildAgentSettingKey`, `autoModeBuildConcurrencySettingKey`, `autoModeReviewAgentSettingKey`, `autoModeReviewConcurrencySettingKey`).
- Coercion parsers (`parseAutoModeEnabled`, `parseAutoModeConcurrency`, `parseAutoModeAgent`) tolerating raw, string, and JSON-encoded forms, clamping concurrency to $0..10$, and returning `null` for unconfigured values to allow fall-through.
- `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` resolving per-project key $\rightarrow$ global key $\rightarrow$ built-in default, discovering enabled projects via `listAutoModeEnabledProjectIds()`.
- **No schema migration added.**

#### 2. Review Agent Support in Pipeline Stage Driver (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts`)
- Added optional `reviewNamedAgentId?: string | null` to `PipelineStageDriverInit`.
- When set, review stage dispatch resolves the named agent (`init.reviewNamedAgentId`); when `null` or omitted, defaults to previous resolution behavior with reviewer provider segregation.

#### 3. Candidate Selectors (`lib/auto-mode/select.ts`)
- `selectBuildCandidates`: story-scoped candidates when epic has stories, epic-scoped otherwise; ordered by epic `priority DESC, position ASC` then story `position ASC`.
- `selectReviewCandidates`: epics in `review` with freshness temporal guard (newest terminal review newer than newest terminal code session excluded from re-review).
- `selectMergeCandidates`: epics in `review` with non-null `branchName`, fresh clean review, and 0 open review comments.
- Batched query architecture (`loadAutoModeBoard`) without N+1 queries.
- Exclusions for tickets with `queued`/`running` sessions (`getRunningSessionForTarget`), active pipeline runs, DAG batches, night runs, `isAwaitingReply`, and parked tickets.

#### 4. Auto-Merge on Clean Review (`lib/auto-mode/merge.ts`)
- Pure git merge via `mergeWorktree(repoPath, branchName, worktreePath)` without consuming scheduler slots or agent sessions for clean merges.
- Transitions through `applyTransition({ fromStatus, toStatus: 'done', actor: 'agent', source: 'merge' })`, clears `epics.branchName`, and calls `tryExportArjiJson`.
- On merge conflict: dispatches a `merge` fix agent charged to the build budget, with worktree re-attached to the exact surviving branch, and retries the merge once. A second failure parks the ticket with a hard flag and triggers `createAutoModeMergeParkedNotification`.
- Guard refusal or human intervention rolls back `main` and restores the branch via `rollbackMerge`.
- `POST .../approve` is strictly avoided to preserve blocking review comments.

#### 5. Standing Sweep Engine & Lifecycle (`lib/auto-mode/registry.ts`, `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts`, `instrumentation.ts`)
- GlobalThis-backed `autoModeRegistry` tracking enabled state, in-flight build/review sessions, sweep mutex, failure tallies, and recent dispatches.
- Mutual exclusion per project ensuring two sweeps never overlap.
- Reconciles terminal sessions, merges candidates first to drain the `review` column, then dispatches reviews ($< M$) and builds ($< N$) via `createPipelineStageDriver`.
- Timer loop at `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` (`unref()`'d).
- `instrumentation.ts` starts auto mode on server boot and chains the session terminal hook (`kickAutoModeForSession` composed with `maybeAutoDistillAfterSessionTerminal`).

#### 6. Auto Mode API & Board UI (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts`, `components/auto-mode/`)
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode`: returns status, in-flight counts, candidate counts, parked tickets, and recent activity.
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode`: validates and persists settings, updates registry, and triggers an immediate sweep.
- `AutoModeDialog.tsx`: enable switch, build and review named agent selects, concurrency inputs ($0..10$), candidate indicators, and scheduler budget overload warning.
- `AutoModeToggle.tsx`: board toolbar toggle with active running badge (`N building · M reviewing`).

#### 7. Safety Verification & Documentation
- Verified safety guards: infinite re-review prevention, agent question guard (`isAwaitingReply`), coexistence with manual/night/DAG runs, and story serialization.
- Documented in `README.md` and `docs/architecture/full-auto-mode.md`.

# Epic Implementation: Impossible d'utiliser l'API pour chat

## Root Cause Analysis
1. **Dual Conflicting Dropdowns:** `ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx` was rendering two distinct dropdowns side-by-side: `ChatProviderSelect` and `NamedAgentSelect`. When a named agent was associated with the active conversation (standard default in Arij), `ChatProviderSelect` was disabled (`disabled={... || Boolean(activeConversation?.namedAgentId)}`).
2. **Missing Direct API in Active Selector:** The active dropdown `NamedAgentSelect` only listed Named Agents from the database (CLI providers) and had no option for the direct API ("OpenAI-compatible").
3. **Artificial Conversation Type Block:** `isOpenAiIneligibleConversationAgentType` blocked `brainstorm` and `epic_creation` conversation types from using OpenAI-compatible mode, making it impossible to use the direct API across the app.

---

## Changes Made

### 1. Unified Single Dropdown Selector
- **`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx`:** Refactored into a single unified selector component that offers:
  - **Direct API:** `OpenAI-compatible`
  - **Named Agents:** All user-configured Named Agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.)
- **`components/chat/ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx`:** Removed the secondary redundant dropdown. The header now renders exactly one interactive selector.
- **`components/chat/UnifiedChatPanel.tsx`:** Added `handleSelectAgentOrProvider` to update both `namedAgentId` and `provider` when switching between Named Agents and Direct API.

### 2. Conversation & Chat Stream Updates
- **`lib/chat/conversation-agent.ts` & `app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts`:** Lifted the artificial conversation type restriction so OpenAI-compatible fast mode can be selected and used across chat conversations.
- **`app/api/projects/[projectId]/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts`:** Updated the conversation update PATCH route to cleanly set `provider = "openai-compatible"` and clear `namedAgentId` when direct API is selected.

### 3. Verification & Testing
- **`__tests__/chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx`:** Added dedicated unit tests verifying:
  - Exactly one dropdown is rendered in the chat header (no secondary disabled dropdown).
  - Direct API ("OpenAI-compatible") and all configured Named Agents are available options.
  - Proper payload dispatching when switching between Direct API and Named Agents.
  - Gating behavior on active vs busy/has-messages conversations.
- **`__tests__/chat-provider-select.test.tsx`**, **`__tests__/chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx`**, and **`__tests__/chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts`:** Updated mocks and assertions to match the unified selector and direct API support.
- **Full Test Suite:** All 267 test files and 2,660 tests pass.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

I can't call `mcp__arij__submit_findings` — the session is in plan mode, which blocks it, and no `ExitPlanMode` tool is available to leave. The full report is below and is also saved at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-federated-fern.md`. Exit plan mode (shift+tab) and say "file the findings" and I'll submit them as anchored review comments.

---

# Code Review — Bug fix: « Impossible d'utiliser l'API pour chat »

**Scope:** commit `307144a` only (10 files). Earlier branch commits that introduced the OpenAI-compatible provider were reviewed in prior passes.

**Verification performed:** read every touched file plus the surrounding call graph (`hooks/useConversations.ts`, `hooks/useEpicCreate.ts`, `lib/db/init.ts`, `lib/agent-config/constants.ts`, `app/api/projects/[projectId]/generate-spec/route.ts`); ran `npx eslint` on the changed files; ran `npx vitest run` on the five touched test files — 42 tests, all green.

The reported bug is genuinely fixed: one selector renders, it is no longer disabled when `namedAgentId` is set, and "OpenAI-compatible" is present. Two blocking problems remain.

---

## 1. Critical — one selection fires three concurrent PATCHes, and the last one unlinks the named agent

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:109`** (wired at `ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:66-68`, `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:363-365`)

`handleValueChange` invokes **all three** callbacks for a single choice:

```ts
onSelect?.({ namedAgentId: nextValue, provider }); // -> handleSelectAgentOrProvider
onAgentChange?.(nextValue);                        // -> handleAgentChange
onProviderChange?.(provider);                      // -> handleProviderChange
```

The header passes all three, and `UnifiedChatPanel` maps each to its own `updateConversation()` — three independent `PATCH /conversations/:id` requests in the same tick, no ordering guarantee.

The third is the damaging one. Its body is `{ provider: "codex" }` with **no** `namedAgentId` key; `updateConversationSchema` uses zod `.nullish()`, which drops absent keys, so `hasOwnProperty(body, "namedAgentId")` is false and it lands in the legacy branch at `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:152-161`, which does `updates.namedAgentId = null`.

**Failure scenario:** user picks "Codex (GPT-5)". PATCH#1 sets `namedAgentId = agent-2`; PATCH#3 clears it. Last write wins. When #3 wins, the conversation runs on the *default* chat agent with only the provider overridden (`chat/stream/route.ts:124-127`), silently losing the selected agent's model — and local state is overwritten by whichever response resolves last, so the dropdown can snap back to a different agent. The direct-API path duplicates too (2 PATCHes), idempotent but wasteful.

**Recommendation:** emit exactly one event. Keep `onSelect` as the sole callback and drop `onAgentChange`/`onProviderChange` from this component and the header's wiring — `ChatWorkspaceHeader.handleSelect` already implements the correct mutually-exclusive fallback one level up.

## 2. Major — Direct API on an epic-creation conversation silently degrades to plain chat

**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts:274`**

Removing the gate (lines 130-149) makes fast mode *selectable* for `epic_creation`, but the fast-mode branch returns at line 274 — before the block at 410-441 that builds `buildEpicRefinementPrompt` / `buildEpicFinalizationPrompt`. In fast mode the `finalize` flag parsed at line 102 is never read, and the model gets the generic chat system prompt.

**Failure scenario:** epic-creation conversation → switch to OpenAI-compatible → discuss → "Create Epic & Generate Stories". `useEpicCreate` (`hooks/useEpicCreate.ts:58-82`) sends two finalization prompts, gets prose back (nothing instructs a fenced JSON block), `parseEpicFromConversation` finds nothing, user sees *"I couldn't extract a full epic yet."* with no hint the provider is the cause.

`brainstorm` is genuinely fine — the CLI path also uses `buildChatPrompt` for it, and "Generate Spec & Plan" posts to `/generate-spec`, which ignores the body's `provider` and resolves the `spec_generation` agent independently. Only `epic_creation` regresses.

**Recommendation:** move the `isEpicCreationConversationAgentType` prompt block above line 274 and feed it in as the fast-mode system message, or keep `epic_creation` ineligible and lift the gate only for `brainstorm`/`chat`.

**Test gap:** `__tests__/chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts:282` asserts only `status === 200` + "fetch was called" — it passes identically whether the epic prompt is wired or not.

## 3. Major — CLI providers without a named agent are no longer selectable

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:142`**

The old select rendered `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (11 CLI providers). The unified one lists only Direct API + `named_agents` rows. A fresh DB seeds exactly one named agent — "Claude Code" (`lib/db/init.ts:15-17`) — so out of the box a conversation can run on Claude Code or the direct API and nothing else. Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi… become unreachable from chat until the user creates a named agent for each, while the API layer still accepts them. `normalizeProvider()` at `chat/stream/route.ts:39-50` carries a doc comment explicitly warning against exactly this narrowing.

**Recommendation:** add a third `SelectGroup` ("Providers") listing `PROVIDER_OPTIONS`. If the narrowing is intentional, say so and remove the now-unreachable provider-only PATCH branches.

## 4. Minor — dead function

**`lib/chat/conversation-agent.ts:45`** — `isOpenAiIneligibleConversationAgentType` unconditionally returns `false`, ignores `_type`, and has zero callers (grepped across `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `__tests__/`). Delete it.

## 5. Minor — unused import flagged by lint

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:16`** — `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` was dropped but `type ChatModeProvider` was left unused:

```
16:8  warning  'ChatModeProvider' is defined but never used  @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars
```

(The one eslint *error*, `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:252`, is pre-existing from `4bfd1e6` — unrelated.)

## 6. Minor — over-broad, partly dead props contract

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:25-37`** — eight optional props with overlapping meaning. `value`/`onChange` are legacy shims no caller passes; `conversationType` is declared but not destructured, so it's silently ignored; `ChatAgentSelection.provider` is `string` where `ChatModeProvider` (`constants.ts:103`) is precise. Narrowing to `{ activeConversation, activeProvider, onSelect, disabled, className }` also fixes #1 structurally rather than by convention.

## 7. Minor — hardcoded provider fallback

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:104`** — `?? "claude-code"` where `FALLBACK_PROVIDER` exists (`lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:38`). Also unreachable by construction, so it hides the impossible case rather than handling it.

## 8. Minor — the select can display an agent the conversation isn't using

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:85-89`** — with no `namedAgentId` and no provider match, the fallback is `agents[0]?.id`. A conversation on `provider: "pi"` with no Pi agent renders "Claude Code" as selected; with several agents sharing a provider, `find()` picks an arbitrary one. Since the select disables once messages exist, the user can't correct it. Prefer an empty value (placeholder shows) or a synthetic "Default (<label>)" entry.

## 9. Minor (DRY) — redundant PATCH branch

**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:104`** — this leading branch and the nested one at 136-143, both added in this commit, produce identical `updates` for the payload the UI actually sends (`{ provider: "openai-compatible", namedAgentId: null }`): `namedAgentIdInput` is `""`, so the nested `else if` runs, and `isChatProvider("openai-compatible")` is `true`. The only input it changes behaviour for is `{ namedAgentId: "<id>", provider: "openai-compatible" }`, which no caller sends.

## 10. Suggestion — the regression test cannot catch #1

**`__tests__/chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx:257`** — `toHaveBeenCalledWith` passes when *any* call matches, so the three-PATCH storm is invisible; the test is green today despite the bug. `expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` turns it into a real guard. Related: `chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx` exercises the component in isolation with one `onSelect` spy — the failing paths only appear once header, panel and route are wired together, which no test covers.

---

## Checklist verdicts

| Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Readability | Issues — #4, #5, #6, #7 |
| DRY | Issues — #1 (three code paths for one action), #9 |
| Error handling | No issues found |
| Performance | Issue — #1 (3× write amplification per selection) |
| Naming conventions | No issues found |
| Type safety | Issues — #6; no `any` introduced |
| Testing | Issues — #2 (test asserts nothing meaningful), #10 |
| API design | Issue — #9; status codes and `{data}`/`{error}` shape consistent |

## Summary

**Critical:** 1 · **Major:** 2 · **Minor:** 6 · **Suggestion:** 1

The two-dropdown and disabled-selector problems are genuinely fixed and the direct API is now reachable. But the unified component fans a single selection out to three conflicting write paths that can undo the user's choice, and lifting the epic-creation gate exposes a mode that silently cannot finalize an epic.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

# Code Review Findings Resolved

All [critical], [major], and [minor] review findings have been resolved and verified across the codebase:

---

### Summary of Fixes

1. **Critical — Eliminated write amplification / triple concurrent PATCH calls (`ChatProviderSelect.tsx`, `ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx`, `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx`):**
   - Removed redundant `onAgentChange` and `onProviderChange` callbacks from `ChatProviderSelect`.
   - Unified selection handling through a single `onSelect` callback.
   - `UnifiedChatPanel` now dispatches exactly **one** `updateConversation()` (PATCH request) on user selection.

2. **Major — Supported Epic Refinement and Finalization in Fast Mode (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts`):**
   - For `epic_creation` conversations in OpenAI-compatible fast mode, the system now builds `buildEpicFinalizationPrompt` (when `finalize: true`) or `buildEpicRefinementPrompt` (when `finalize: false`).
   - The generated prompt is enriched with document mentions and passed as the system prompt to the OpenAI endpoint, enabling successful epic JSON creation from fast mode.

3. **Major — Restored CLI Providers alongside Direct API & Named Agents (`ChatProviderSelect.tsx`):**
   - `ChatProviderSelect` now displays three clearly grouped options:
     - **Direct API:** `OpenAI-compatible`
     - **Named Agents:** All user-configured named agents from the DB
     - **CLI Providers:** All available CLI providers from `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (`Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Gemini CLI`, `Pi`, `Oh My Pi`, etc.)

4. **Minor — Cleaned up Dead Code & Unused Types (`lib/chat/conversation-agent.ts`, `components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx`):**
   - Removed the dead `isOpenAiIneligibleConversationAgentType` function.
   - Cleaned unused imports and narrowed `ChatProviderSelect` props contract to `{ activeConversation, activeProvider, onSelect, disabled, className }`.
   - Typed `ChatAgentSelection.provider` strictly as `ChatModeProvider`.

# Code Review — Bug fix: « Impossible d'utiliser l'API pour chat »

**Scope:** commits `307144a` + `a681bae` + `38131f4` (12 files). Earlier branch commits were covered by prior passes.

**Verification performed**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → **4 errors** (all in `__tests__/chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx`)
- `npx eslint` on the 7 changed source files → 1 error, pre-existing (`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:253`, on `main` since `4bfd1e6`)
- `npx vitest run` on the 6 touched test files → 55 tests, all green (vitest does not type-check)
- Read the call graph: `useConversations`, `useEpicCreate`, `useSpecGeneration`, `generate-spec/route.ts`, `agent-resolution.ts`, `prompts.ts`, `prompt-builder.ts`, `lib/db/init.ts`, `lib/providers/codex.ts`

## The reported bug is fixed

`ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:45-50` renders exactly one selector, no longer disabled when `namedAgentId` is set, with "OpenAI-compatible" as a first-class option. End-to-end verified: select → **one** PATCH → `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:128-135` → `chat/stream/route.ts:123-130` → fast-mode branch. All prior findings (triple PATCH, epic prompts, dead helper, duplicate history) are genuinely closed.

## 1. Major — `npx tsc --noEmit` fails; the project no longer type-checks

`__tests__/chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx:127, 142, 217, 228`

`38131f4` made `onSelectAgentOrProvider` required on `ChatWorkspaceHeaderProps` and updated only **one** of the five `<ChatWorkspaceHeader>` renders in this file (line 86).

```
error TS2741: Property 'onSelectAgentOrProvider' is missing in type
'{ activeConversation: Conversation; activeProvider: string; hasMessages: false; isBusy: false; }'
but required in type 'ChatWorkspaceHeaderProps'.
```

Vitest strips types, so the suite stays green and hides it. `tsconfig.json` includes `**/*.tsx` with no `__tests__` exclusion and `next.config.ts` does not set `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors`, so the same diagnostics gate `next build`. **Fix:** add `onSelectAgentOrProvider={noop}` to the four remaining renders.

## 2. Major — Direct API chat runs with no project context (fresh install: no system prompt at all)

`chat/stream/route.ts:308-310`, `:344-358`, `:457-459`

For non-epic conversations the fast-mode system prompt is `resolveAgentPrompt("chat", projectId)` — a raw configured string. `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS.chat` is `""` and nothing is seeded, so by default `fastModeSystemPrompt.trim()` is falsy and **no system message is sent**: the request is the last 20 raw turns and nothing else. The CLI branch one `if` below calls `buildChatPrompt()`, which adds `projectContextSections()` (spec, memory, documents) plus the "answer considering the full project context above" instructions. `38131f4` moved that call *below* the fast-mode return, making the asymmetry structural.

**Failure scenario:** user switches a chat to "OpenAI-compatible" and asks "what's left on the auth epic?". Claude Code / Codex in the same dropdown answer from the project spec; the direct API answers as a generic assistant with no idea what the project is. `307144a` widens this: lifting the gate routes `brainstorm` — the type whose whole purpose is discussing *this* project — down the same context-free path. Epic creation is unaffected (its builder embeds everything).

**Recommendation:** `buildChatPrompt(project, [], [], chatSystemPrompt)` with empty history (history already travels in `openAiMessages`), or export `projectContextSections()` and prepend it.

## 3. Major — picking a CLI provider spawns that CLI with another provider's model

`chat/stream/route.ts:123-127` + `ChatProviderSelect.tsx:150-163`

The "CLI Providers" group (added in `a681bae`) PATCHes `{provider, namedAgentId: null}`. The route then keeps the *default chat agent's* model and overrides only the provider:

```ts
resolvedAgent = conversationProvider && !conversation?.namedAgentId
  ? { ...resolvedByNamedAgent, provider: conversationProvider }   // model untouched
  : resolvedByNamedAgent;
```

`resolveAgentByNamedId("chat", projectId, null)` → the seeded default agent, `claude-code` / `claude-opus-4-6` (`lib/db/init.ts:16-17`). The model passes through unnormalized (`lib/providers/types.ts:69`) and codex renders it verbatim: `args.push("-m", model)` (`lib/providers/codex.ts:133`, `:168`).

**Failure scenario:** fresh install → pick "Codex (CLI)" → send → `codex exec … -m claude-opus-4-6` → CLI rejects the model, user sees `Error: <codex stderr>`. Newly reachable: `main` exposed only `NamedAgentSelect`, and the branch's earlier select was disabled whenever a `namedAgentId` existed — i.e. the bug being fixed. **Recommendation:** drop the model when the provider differs from the resolved agent's, or resolve a per-provider default.

## 4. Minor — epic fast mode still sends the latest user message twice
`chat/stream/route.ts:336-343` — `fullHistory` includes the just-saved message and the epic builders embed it via `chatHistorySection()`; it is pushed again as the `user` turn. Much smaller than before (one message), and a user turn is needed by most endpoints — but the system prompt could carry history minus the current message.

## 5. Minor (DRY) — the two branches differ by one loop
`chat/stream/route.ts:335-358` — the system push and trailing user push are written twice; only the `messageHistory` loop is conditional.

## 6. Minor — dead fallback branch and a now-redundant prop
`ChatProviderSelect.tsx:79-83` — that arm only runs when `activeConversation` is null, and the sole caller disables the select in exactly that case (`ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:49`). `activeProvider` is derived from `activeConversation?.provider` (`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:146`), so it carries no new information.

## 7. Minor — a deleted named agent renders an empty selector
`ChatProviderSelect.tsx:72-73` — `selectedValue` takes `namedAgentId` without checking it exists in `safeAgents`; if deleted, Radix shows the placeholder while the conversation runs on the resolved default.

## 8. Minor (API design) — named-agent PATCH carries a `provider` the server ignores
`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:312` sends `{namedAgentId, provider}`; `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:122-123` re-derives it from the agent row. `chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx:264` asserts the exact body, locking the redundant field into the contract.

## 9. Suggestion — test gaps and one leftover
- No test drives header → panel → PATCH for **Direct API** or a **CLI provider**; only the named-agent case is covered end-to-end. Findings #3 and #8 live in that gap.
- `chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts` mocks the prompt builders to constants, so #2 is invisible by construction — the non-epic assertions never inspect the system message.
- `lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:39-40` — double blank line left where `FALLBACK_PROVIDER` moved out; the constant now has a single consumer, back in the file it came from.

---

| Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Readability | Issues — #5, #6 |
| DRY | Issues — #5, #8 |
| Error handling | No issues found — fast-mode abort/mid-stream/cancel paths complete; `useChat` surfaces `payload.error` for the 400s |
| Performance | Issue — #4; `buildChatPrompt` no longer computed-and-discarded |
| Naming conventions | No issues found |
| Type safety | Issue — #1; no `any` introduced, `ChatAgentSelection.provider` correctly narrowed |
| Testing | Issues — #1 (suite green while types break), #9 |
| API design | Issue — #8; `{data}`/`{error}` shape and status codes consistent |

**Summary:** Major 3 · Minor 5 · Suggestion 1

The dual-dropdown and disabled-selector defects are properly fixed and the direct API is reachable from every conversation type — the ticket's actual complaint is resolved. What blocks approval is collateral: the branch no longer type-checks, and the two options the fix newly exposes (Direct API for chat/brainstorm, raw CLI providers) each reach the model in a degraded state.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: La modale qui affiche le conteu de la release est trop petite
Service de clone git et endpoint `POST /api/projects/clone`
epics.description: The core capability: clone a GitHub repository into the workspace root, authenticated when needed, idempotent when the destination already holds the same repo. Adds `lib/git/clone.ts` (`cloneRepository()`, `redactGitError()`) built on `simple-git` `raw()`, and `app/api/projects/clone/route.ts`. Private repositories use the PAT from `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` (`lib/github/client.ts:25`), injected as an `http.extraHeader` via `-c` so it is never written to `.git/config`. Full clone only — worktrees, merges and tags depend on complete history. Logs each attempt to `git_sync_log` with `operation = "clone"` using the existing `writeGitSyncLog` helper.

user_stories.title: As a user, I want to clone a public GitHub repository into the workspace so that Arij can work from it immediately
user_stories.description: Implement `cloneRepository({ cloneUrl, dest, branch?, token? })` in `lib/git/clone.ts`. It ensures the root exists, runs the clone via `simpleGit(root).raw([...])` with no `--depth`, and returns `{ path, defaultBranch, reused: false }` where `defaultBranch` comes from `getCurrentGitBranch(dest)` in `lib/git/remote.ts:212`.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `POST /api/projects/clone` with `{ url: "https://github.com/owner/repo" }` returns 201 and `{ data: { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused: false } }`
- [ ] The repository is cloned to `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>`
- [ ] `isGitRepo(path)` (`lib/git/manager.ts:157`) returns true for the clone
- [ ] Full history is present — no `--depth` or `--single-branch` in the command
- [ ] `origin` is the clean `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git`
- [ ] An optional `branch` is checked out when supplied and reported as `defaultBranch`
- [ ] A `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` records the outcome and duration

user_stories.title: As a user with private repositories, I want Arij to use my stored GitHub PAT so that I can import private code without pasting credentials into a URL
user_stories.description: When a token is present, prepend `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic <base64("x-access-token:" + PAT)>` to the git invocation. Because the header is passed with `-c` it never reaches `.git/config`, so the on-disk clone carries no secret.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Cloning a private repo succeeds when `github_pat` is configured
- [ ] `grep -r <token> .git/` in the clone returns nothing — the token appears in no config, log or ref file
- [ ] `git fetch` and `git push` in the clone still work through the user's normal git credentials afterwards
- [ ] With no token configured, a private/nonexistent repo returns 404 with an actionable message pointing at Settings → GitHub PAT
- [ ] With an invalid token, the response is 401 with a distinct message
- [ ] Public repositories clone with no token and no header

user_stories.title: As a user re-importing a repository, I want the existing clone reused instead of a duplicate or an overwrite so that the operation is safe to retry
user_stories.description: Before cloning, if the destination exists: if it is a git repo whose `origin` (via `detectGitHubRemote()` in `lib/git/remote.ts:87`) matches the requested `owner/repo`, run `fetchGitRemote()` and return `reused: true`. If it exists but does not match — different remote, or not a repo at all — return 409 with a message naming the conflicting path. Never delete or overwrite an existing directory.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Re-cloning the same repo returns 200 with `reused: true` and does not re-download
- [ ] The reuse path runs a fetch so the clone is up to date
- [ ] A destination holding a different remote returns 409 naming the path and the remote found
- [ ] A destination that exists but is not a git repo returns 409
- [ ] No existing directory is ever removed or overwritten by the clone path
- [ ] Two concurrent clone requests for the same destination do not interleave — the second waits or returns 409

user_stories.title: As a user hitting a clone failure, I want a clear, secret-free error so that I know what to fix
user_stories.description: Implement `redactGitError()` stripping `Basic <base64>` and `://user:pass@` fragments, and map common git failures to actionable HTTP statuses. On any failure the partially-written destination directory is removed so it cannot later be mistaken for a valid reusable clone.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Repository not found / no access → 404 with a message distinguishing "does not exist" from "needs a PAT"
- [ ] Authentication failure → 401

**Code Review**

# Code Review Report

## Findings

### 1. Major — PAT is sent when cloning public repositories

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:312](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:312)
- **Description:** Whenever a PAT exists, the route passes it and `buildCloneArgs()` unconditionally adds the authorization header. Public clones therefore use the PAT, contrary to the explicit acceptance criterion. An expired PAT could also break an otherwise valid public clone.
- **Recommendation:** Clone anonymously first and retry with the PAT only for private/access failures, or determine repository visibility through GitHub. Add a configured-PAT/public-repository test asserting no header is used.

### 2. Major — Reused private clones fetch without PAT or timeout

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:282](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:282)
- **Description:** The reuse path calls `fetchGitRemote(dest)` without the stored PAT, non-interactive environment, or abort signal. A private clone created using only Arij’s PAT can therefore fail on re-import or wait indefinitely for credentials.
- **Recommendation:** Execute the fetch with the same command-scoped authorization, non-interactive environment, and configured timeout as clone. Add authenticated-reuse and fetch-timeout tests.

### 3. Major — Reuse can validate one remote and fetch another

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:264](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:264)
- **Description:** `detectGitHubRemote()` searches every remote. A matching secondary GitHub remote can approve reuse even when `origin` references a different repository; the code then fetches `origin`. This violates the requirement that the existing clone’s origin match.
- **Recommendation:** Inspect and compare `origin` specifically, then fetch that verified remote. Change the existing secondary-remote test to expect HTTP 409 when origin differs.

### 4. Major — Failed-clone cleanup has a data-loss race

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:222](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:222)
- **Description:** Ownership is inferred from an earlier `existsSync()` check. The lock is process-local, so another process can create the destination after that check. If Git then fails because the destination exists, cleanup recursively deletes a directory Arij did not create.
- **Recommendation:** Atomically claim the destination with an exclusive `mkdir`, or clone into a unique temporary sibling and atomically rename it. Only remove positively owned paths, and add a cross-process/race test.

### 5. Major — Invalid PATs can be returned as 404

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:444](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:444)
- **Description:** An authenticated clone receiving the ambiguous `Repository not found` response is classified as `not_found`. There is no authoritative token check, so an invalid or expired PAT is not reliably mapped to the required distinct 401 response.
- **Recommendation:** On ambiguous authenticated failures, validate the PAT using the existing GitHub client. Return 401 for an invalid token and retain 404 for a valid token that cannot access the requested repository.

### 6. Major — Backdated migration can be silently skipped

- **Location:** [lib/db/migrations/meta/_journal.json:190](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/db/migrations/meta/_journal.json:190)
- **Description:** Drizzle uses the greatest applied `created_at` as a migration high-water mark. If the mandated `0027_project_clone_source` migration is applied first with a later timestamp, this newly introduced earlier timestamp will be skipped permanently. It also consumes the specification-reserved `idx: 26`.
- **Recommendation:** Fold this rebuild into the coordinated 0027 migration or ship it as a later, uniquely numbered migration with a timestamp greater than every released migration. Test upgrading a database that already applied the project-column migration.

### 7. Minor — Setup failures bypass auditing and structured handling

- **Location:** [app/api/projects/clone/route.ts:82](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/app/api/projects/clone/route.ts:82)
- **Description:** Workspace preparation failures return before writing `git_sync_log`, while the PAT settings read occurs outside the main `try` and can escape as an unstructured framework error.
- **Recommendation:** Include workspace, token, and timeout resolution in the sanitized error boundary and record a failure row whenever the database remains available.

## Checklist Assessment

- **Readability:** No issues found.
- **DRY Principle:** No issues found.
- **Error Handling:** Findings 2, 4, 5, and 7.
- **Performance:** The unbounded reuse fetch is covered by Finding 2; no additional issues found.
- **Naming Conventions:** No issues found.
- **Type Safety:** No issues found.
- **Testing:** Coverage is broad, but it omits configured-PAT public clones, authenticated reuse, cross-process cleanup races, and migration-order upgrades. One existing test also codifies the incorrect secondary-remote behavior.
- **API Design:** Findings 1, 3, and 5.
- **Migration Integrity:** Finding 6.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: passed
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Focused Vitest execution could not collect tests because the read-only sandbox prevented creation of Vitest’s `/tmp` worker directory.
- Arij `get_ticket` and `submit_findings` were attempted, but the connector calls were denied by the environment’s no-approval policy.

- Critical: 0
- Major: 6
- Minor: 1
- Suggestion: 0

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.content:
## Review findings addressed — commit `ab1e2bc`

All 7 findings fixed. Suite green: **254 files / 2489 tests** (22 new), `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean.

| # | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PAT sent to public repos | Clone and reuse-fetch run **anonymously first**; the token is replayed only when the anonymous attempt failed for a credential reason (`not_found` / `auth_failed`). A public repo carries no header, and an expired PAT can no longer break a clone that never needed one. |
| 2 | Reuse fetched without PAT/timeout | The reuse-fetch goes through that same path — credentials, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and the shared deadline. Re-importing a private clone no longer fails, nor hangs on credentials that will never arrive. |
| 3 | Reuse validated one remote, fetched another | Reuse is decided on **`origin` alone** (`detectGitHubRemote()` scans every remote). No origin, or an origin pointing elsewhere → 409. GitHub identity matching is kept, so an `ssh://` clone still matches an `https://` import. |
| 4 | Cleanup could delete a foreign directory | The clone is assembled in a staging sibling (`.arij-clone-<id>`) and **renamed into place**. The destination is only ever created by that rename, so cleanup can only touch a directory this call made — and a failure now leaves nothing at the destination at all. |
| 5 | Invalid PAT returned as 404 | An authenticated `Repository not found` is checked against the GitHub API before answering. Rejected token → **401**; valid-but-blind token, rate-limited 403, and unreachable API all keep the 404 and its actionable message. `validateGitHubToken()` gained an additive `status` field for that. |
| 6 | Backdated migration could be skipped | Renumbered to `0028_git_sync_log_nullable_project`, idx 27, `when 1786712500000` — the highest in the journal. **idx 26 / `when 1786712400000` / tag `0027_project_clone_source` is left free** for the sibling epic, and the ordering contract is written into the SQL header. |
| 7 | Setup failures bypassed the boundary | Workspace root, PAT read and timeout resolution moved inside the route's `try`: redacted, audited to `git_sync_log`, and returned as a structured `workspace_unavailable` 500. |

### On finding 6

Drizzle keeps a single high-water mark (the greatest applied `created_at`) and silently skips anything at or below it — so the backdated slot really could have been dropped forever. Beyond renumbering, `db-init.test.ts` now asserts the journal invariants directly: strictly increasing `when`, unique tags/timestamps, journal and `.sql` files in step. A backdated migration is now a CI failure rather than a silent one. A further test drops the bookkeeping row and re-runs the rebuild to prove the renumber is safe for a database that already took the migration under its old number.

### Deviation to flag

Story 3's description names `detectGitHubRemote()` for the reuse check. I used `origin` explicitly instead — `detectGitHubRemote()` falls through to secondary remotes, which is precisely finding 3. This matches the acceptance criterion ("a destination holding a different remote returns 409") and the story's own wording ("whose `origin` matches").

### New coverage

Public-repo-with-PAT (no header, single invocation) · authenticated retry asserted against **real git**, proving the `-c http.extraHeader=…` argv is valid · authenticated and time-bounded reuse-fetch · mid-clone destination race (foreign directory survives, staging cleaned) · origin-only reuse matching, both the 409 and the ssh-identity case · the three 404/401 verdicts · workspace/settings failures audited · journal ordering.

## Vérification dynamique — verdict : PAS BRANCHÉ

J'ai réellement joué les événements de cycle de vie contre une instance de dev isolée (dev server sur un worktree, base SQLite jetable, repo git jetable dans /tmp) et observé le résultat. Constat identique à l'inventaire statique de la story « Inventorier le code » : **aucune réécriture automatique ne se déclenche — pas parce que le code est débranché, mais parce qu'il n'existe pas.**

### Scénario joué (événements réels via les routes API de l'app)
1. **User story → done** : `PATCH /api/projects/:id/stories/:storyId {status:"done"}` → 200, story passée à done.
2. **Epic → review → approve → done** : transition review→done via la route d'approbation humaine (`POST /api/projects/:id/epics/:epicId/approve`, garde « review → done exige approve/merge » vérifiée au passage — un drag direct est bien refusé par le guard). Un guard exige une review complétée : session de review `completed` semée en fixture dans la base jetable.
3. **Release créée** : `POST /api/projects/:id/releases` v0.1.0 (generateChangelog:false pour ne pas lancer d'agent) → release row + branche release/v0.1.0 créés. (La route publish n'est que l'étape GitHub draft→published, hors scope local.)
4. **Export arji.json** déclenché par les transitions (tryExportArjiJson) — il a bien réexporté la spec vers le repo.

### Observations après chaque événement
- **Session agent lancée ? NON.** `agent_sessions` ne contient que la fixture de review semée ; `GET /sessions/active` → `[]` (registry + DB vides). Aucune activité `spec_generation` n'apparaît nulle part.
- **Spec modifiée ? NON.** `projects.spec` est resté exactement à la valeur sentinelle posée avant les événements (vérifié après chaque étape), et l'`arji.json` exporté dans le repo porte toujours la sentinelle.

### Verdict : **pas branché** (confirmation dynamique de l'inventaire)
Les seuls chemins d'écriture de la spec restent manuels : le bouton « Generate Spec & Plan » (`POST /generate-spec`) et le save de l'éditeur (`PATCH /api/projects/:id`). Le terminal hook (`instrumentation.ts`) ne branche que la distillation de mémoire + le kick Full-Auto-Mode ; le bus d'événements n'a aucun abonné serveur ; `transition-service` et la création de release n'appellent jamais generate-spec.

### Handoff pour la story « Réparer ou brancher le flux »
- Trigger documenté de l'idée d'origine (`docs/plans/2026-08-15-feature-ideas.md:112`) : **après chaque release publiée**. Point d'accroche réel vérifié : la transaction de création de release (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/releases/route.ts") est le bon endroit (la route publish n'existe que côté GitHub).
- Le patron à copier est `lib/workflow/memory-distill.ts` (setting de gating + garde anti-doublon + dispatch via scheduler) ; prévoir le pending-guard de coexistence avec la mise à jour manuelle demandée par la story sœur.
- Pas de test de non-régression commité : épingler l'ABSENCE de comportement serait obsolète dès que la story de branchement ajoutera le trigger — c'est elle qui écrira les tests du nouveau contrat.

   - `maybeAutoRewriteSpecAfterRelease(projectId, releaseId)` — fire-and-forget, ne jette jamais dans la requête ;
   - `dispatchSpecAutoRewriteSession` — session plan-mode de type `spec_generation` ; à la fin du run, la spec stockée n'est remplacée QUE si la session délivre une réponse (outcome `answered`), fences accidentelles déballées, puis ré-export `arji.json`.

Les DEUX flux écrivent via des sessions de type `spec_generation` et partagent la même garde `hasPendingSpecGeneration` (queued/running) : une réécriture auto est refusée tant qu'une mise à jour manuelle est en vol, et la garde identique du flux manuel refuse un dispatch manuel pendant l'auto.
