epics.title: Unified Chat & Epic Creation Side Panel
epics.description:
Rework the separate chat panel and epic creation flow into a single unified side panel component. The panel lives on the right side of the screen, collapsed by default (showing ~5% as a grayed-out edge). Clicking 'Chat' or 'New Epic' expands the panel, splitting the screen into a resizable two-pane layout (board + chat). The panel supports tabbed conversations with agent activity indicators and mandatory agent type selection on each new chat.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Unified Panel Shell
- Create a `UnifiedChatPanel` component that replaces the current separate chat panel and epic creation chat
- Panel has three visual states: collapsed (5% visible, grayed overlay on the right edge), expanded (resizable split with the board), and hidden (0%)
- Default state is collapsed — a thin vertical strip visible on the right side
- Clicking the collapsed strip or toolbar buttons ('Chat', 'New Epic') transitions to expanded state
- Use a resizable split layout (e.g. `react-resizable-panels` or custom CSS resize) so the user can drag the divider between the board and the chat panel
- Persist the panel width in local state (or localStorage) so it remembers the user's preferred split

### Phase 2 — Tabbed Conversations
- The panel supports multiple open conversations as tabs (similar to browser tabs)
- Each tab represents a chat conversation (brainstorm, epic creation, or general)
- Tabs show the conversation title (truncated) and a close button
- A '+' button creates a new tab
- Active tab is visually highlighted
- Tab state persisted in the existing `chatMessages` / `chatConversations` DB tables

### Phase 3 — Agent Activity Indicator in Tabs
- When an agent is actively working on a conversation (streaming response, building, etc.), display a small animated icon (spinner or pulsing dot) on the corresponding tab
- The indicator is visible even when the panel is collapsed, appearing on the thin right-edge strip as a subtle glow or badge
- Poll agent session status to determine which conversations have active agents

### Phase 4 — Agent Type Selector on New Chat
- When creating a new conversation ('+' tab or 'New Epic' / 'Chat' trigger), show a mandatory agent type selector before the first message
- Agent types: 'Brainstorm' (plan mode), 'Epic Creation' (spec generation mode), or custom types from agent config
- The selected type determines the prompt builder and Claude Code mode used
- Selector displayed as a prominent dropdown or button group at the top of the empty chat
- Once the first message is sent, the agent type is locked for that conversation

### Phase 5 — Board Integration
- Remove the old chat panel toggle from the project header
- The kanban board occupies 100% width when the panel is collapsed
- When expanded, the board flexes to fill the remaining space
- 'New Epic' button in the board toolbar opens the panel with a new 'Epic Creation' tab pre-selected

epics.title: Agent Busy Guards & Visual Feedback
epics.description:
Prevent overlapping agent actions on epics and stories by enforcing busy guards across all action types, and provide clear visual feedback on kanban cards and story views when an agent is actively working.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Unified Agent Busy State Detection
- Create a shared utility/hook `useAgentBusyState(entityId, entityType)` that checks whether any agent session (build, review, chat) is currently running for a given epic or story
- Query the `agentSessions` table for running sessions linked to the entity
- Return `{ isBusy, sessionType, sessionId }` so the UI knows what kind of work is happening
- This replaces the scattered `isRunning` checks with a single source of truth

### Phase 2 — Backend Concurrency Guards
- Add a generic `checkActiveSession(entityId, entityType)` helper in the API layer
- Apply it to ALL agent dispatch endpoints: build, review, send-to-dev, team build, chat
- Return HTTP 409 Conflict with a descriptive message when an agent is already working on the entity
- Ensure the guard checks both epic-level and story-level sessions (e.g., a story build blocks epic-level actions on the same epic's worktree)

### Phase 3 — Kanban Card Busy Indicators
- Add a visual indicator (spinner, pulsing dot, or animated border) on kanban epic cards when an agent is actively working
- Show the type of work in progress (e.g., 'Building...', 'Reviewing...') as a small badge on the card
- The indicator should be visible without opening the epic detail panel
- Poll or use existing session polling to keep the indicator in sync

### Phase 4 — Greyed-Out Actions in Epic & Story Views
- In `EpicActions`, disable ALL agent action buttons (Build, Review, Send to Dev) when any agent session is active for the epic — not just the same action type
- In `StoryActions` and `UserStoryQuickActions`, disable agent action buttons when a session is running for that story or its parent epic's worktree
- Show a tooltip on disabled buttons explaining why (e.g., 'Agent is currently building this epic')
- Replace loading-only disabled state with session-aware disabled state

### Phase 5 — Review Endpoint Concurrency Check
- The review endpoint currently lacks the same concurrency guard as the build endpoint
- Add `checkActiveSession` to the review dispatch route
- Prevent launching multiple overlapping review agents for the same story
- Allow multiple different review types to run in parallel (security + code review) but prevent duplicate types

epics.title: Fuse New Epic into Chat Panel
epics.description:
Remove the standalone 'New Epic' modal/flow and instead open epic creation as a new tab in the existing UnifiedChatPanel. When the user clicks 'New Epic', the chat panel opens with a new tab of type `epic_creation`. The chat stream API route checks the conversation type and uses the epic refinement prompt for `epic_creation` conversations. After the brainstorming chat converges, a 'Create Epic & Generate Stories' button triggers epic + user story creation from the conversation context.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1 — Server-side routing in /api/chat/stream
- Modify the chat stream endpoint to check the conversation's `type` field
- When type is `epic_creation`, use the epic refinement prompt builder (existing `buildSpecPrompt` or a new `buildEpicCreationPrompt`) instead of the default brainstorm prompt
- Ensure the prompt includes project context (spec, documents) and instructs Claude to help the user define an epic with user stories

### Step 2 — New useEpicCreate hook
- Create a small React hook (`useEpicCreate`) that takes the conversation context and calls the API to create an epic with generated user stories
- The hook calls `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/epics` with the epic data extracted from the conversation
- Returns loading/error/success states

### Step 3 — UnifiedChatPanel UI updates
- Add a 'Create Epic & Generate Stories' button that appears in `epic_creation` conversations once enough context has been discussed
- Differentiate tab icons: sparkles icon for `epic_creation` tabs vs message icon for regular chat tabs
- Add an empty-state hint in new `epic_creation` tabs explaining what the user can do
- Wire `onEpicCreated` callback to refresh the kanban board and optionally close the tab

### Step 4 — MessageInput placeholder
- Add a `placeholder` prop to the MessageInput component
- Set context-aware placeholder text: 'Describe your epic idea...' for epic_creation tabs, 'Ask a question...' for brainstorm tabs

### Step 5 — Rewire page.tsx
- Point the 'New Epic' button in the project page to `panelRef.current?.openNewEpic()` which creates a new `epic_creation` tab
- Remove the old modal/sheet import and rendering

### Step 6 — Delete dead code
- Remove `CreateEpicSheet.tsx` component

epics.title: Agent Configuration Side Panel & Custom Review Agents
epics.description:
Dedicated side panel for configuring agent prompts (global + per-project override), creating custom review agents, and setting the default AI provider per agent type.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Schema & Data Layer

**Agent Prompts Table:**
- Add `agentPrompts` table: id, agentType (text: 'build', 'review_security', 'review_code', 'review_compliance', 'chat', 'spec_generation', 'team_build', 'ticket_build'), systemPrompt (text), scope ('global' | projectId), createdAt, updatedAt
- Global prompts have scope='global', project overrides store the projectId
- When resolving a prompt, project-scoped prompt takes precedence over global, which takes precedence over built-in defaults

**Custom Review Agents Table:**
- Add `customReviewAgents` table: id, name (text), systemPrompt (text), scope ('global' | projectId), position (integer), isEnabled (integer, default 1), createdAt, updatedAt
- Custom review agents are user-defined and appear alongside the 3 built-in review types

**Agent Provider Defaults Table:**
- Add `agentProviderDefaults` table: id, agentType (text), provider ('claude-code' | 'codex'), scope ('global' | projectId), createdAt, updatedAt
- Allows setting CC or Codex as default per agent type, with project override

### Phase 2 — API Routes

**Agent Prompts:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/prompts` — list all global agent prompts
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts` — list project-scoped prompts (merged with global defaults)
- `PUT /api/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — upsert global prompt for an agent type
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — upsert project override
- `DELETE /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/prompts/[agentType]` — remove project override (fall back to global)

**Custom Review Agents:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/review-agents` — list global custom review agents
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/review-agents` — list project-scoped + global review agents
- `POST /api/agent-config/review-agents` — create a custom review agent (global)
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/review-agents` — create project-scoped review agent
- `PATCH /api/agent-config/review-agents/[agentId]` — update name, prompt, enabled status
- `DELETE /api/agent-config/review-agents/[agentId]` — delete a custom review agent

**Agent Provider Defaults:**
- `GET /api/agent-config/providers` — list global provider defaults per agent type
- `PUT /api/agent-config/providers/[agentType]` — set global default provider for agent type
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/agent-config/providers/[agentType]` — set project override

### Phase 3 — Prompt Builder Integration
- Refactor all prompt builder functions to load custom prompts from DB before composing
- Resolution order: project override → global custom → built-in default
- Update `buildReviewPrompt` to accept custom review agent prompts in addition to built-in types
- Update `buildBuildPrompt`, `buildChatPrompt`, `buildSpecPrompt`, `buildTeamBuildPrompt`, `buildTicketBuildPrompt` to use configurable prompts

### Phase 4 — Side Panel UI
- New `AgentConfigPanel` component accessible from the main sidebar
- Three tabs: **Agent Prompts**, **Review Agents**, **Provider Defaults**
- Agent Prompts tab: list of agent types with expandable prompt editors, toggle between global/project scope
- Review Agents tab: list of built-in (read-only name) + custom review agents, each with name/prompt fields, add/delete actions
- Provider Defaults tab: per-agent-type dropdown to select CC or Codex as default
- Panel slides in from the left sidebar, can be toggled open/closed

### Phase 5 — Review Dialog Integration
- Update the Agent Review dialog on the story detail page to include custom review agents alongside the 3 built-in types
- Custom agents displayed as additional checkboxes with their name
- Each selected custom agent dispatches a plan-mode agent with the custom prompt
- Agent output posted as a comment with the custom agent's name as label

epics.title: Agent Teams & Codex Provider Integration
epics.description:
Two-part feature: (1) Agent Teams mode that leverages Claude Code's native Task tool to delegate multiple tickets to sub-agents in a single session, and (2) OpenAI Codex integration as an alternative AI provider alongside Claude Code.

## Implementation Plan

### Part A — Agent Teams (Claude Code Only)

**Schema & Data Layer:**
- Add `orchestrationMode` column to `agentSessions` table (`'solo' | 'team'`, default `'solo'`)
- Team mode is exclusive to Claude Code (Codex has no equivalent sub-agent delegation)

**Prompt Builder:**
- New `buildTeamBuildPrompt()` function that describes all selected epics with their worktree paths
- Instructs Claude Code to act as a team lead and use the `Task` tool to spawn sub-agents per ticket
- Lets CC decide team composition and size

**Build Route Changes:**
- When `team=true` in the batch build request, pre-create all git worktrees for selected epics
- Spawn a single CC session from the main repo root (not inside a worktree)
- Add `Task` to the `--allowedTools` list for team mode
- Track as a single `agentSession` with `orchestrationMode: 'team'`
- On completion, update all associated epics' statuses

**UI — Build Toolbar:**
- Add 'Team mode' checkbox in the build toolbar, visible when 2+ epics are selected
- Checkbox disabled when fewer than 2 epics selected or when provider is Codex
- Tooltip explains team mode behavior

### Part B — Codex Provider Integration

**Provider Abstraction Layer:**
- New `lib/providers/` directory with provider interface (`AgentProvider`)
- `lib/providers/claude-code.ts` — wraps existing CC spawn logic

epics.title: Ticket Comments, Send-to-Dev & Agent Review
epics.description:
Add a comment system to user stories (tickets), a dedicated story detail page replacing the sheet, and review workflows powered by Claude Code agents.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Schema & Data Layer
- Add `ticketComments` table (id, userStoryId, author: 'user'|'agent', content, agentSessionId?, createdAt)
- Add `userStoryId` column to `agentSessions` to link agent work back to a specific ticket
- Add `"review"` as a valid status for user stories (todo → in_progress → review → done)

### Phase 2 — API Routes
- `GET/PATCH /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]` — fetch & update story detail
- `GET/POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/comments` — list & add comments
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/build` — dispatch a code-mode agent for the ticket (send-to-dev)
- `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/review` — dispatch review agents (security, code-review, compliance/accessibility)

### Phase 3 — Hooks
- `useStoryDetail` — fetch story with epic context
- `useComments` — fetch comments with 5s polling
- `useTicketAgent` — dispatch agent + poll session status, auto-post final output as agent comment

### Phase 4 — Story Detail Page
- New route: `/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]`
- Two-column layout: left = story details (title, description, acceptance criteria, status, priority), right = comment thread
- Navigate to this page by clicking story titles in the epic detail view

### Phase 5 — Send to Dev
- Available on tickets in `todo` or `in_progress` status
- "Send to Dev" button opens a dialog with an optional comment field
- On confirm: post comment (if provided), dispatch code-mode agent with ticket context + full comment history, move ticket to `in_progress`
- Agent reuses the epic's existing git worktree/branch with concurrency guard

### Phase 6 — Agent Review (Review status)
- Available on tickets in `review` status
- "Send to Dev" button (requires mandatory comment explaining what to fix) → dispatches code agent, moves ticket back to `in_progress`
- "Agent Review" button opens dialog with 3 checkboxes: Security, Code Review, Compliance/Accessibility
- Each selected review type dispatches a separate agent in plan mode with a specialized review checklist
- Agent outputs are posted as comments on the ticket

### Phase 7 — Approve & Merge
- "Approve" action on review-status tickets marks the ticket as `done`
- Triggers merge of the epic's worktree branch into the target branch

### Prompt Builder
- `buildTicketBuildPrompt` — code mode, includes project spec, epic context, ticket details, and full comment history
- `buildReviewPrompt` — plan mode, 3 specialized checklists (security audit, code review best practices, compliance/accessibility standards)

epics.title: Chat Image Upload & Clipboard Paste
epics.description:
Add image support to chat panels — users can upload images via a file picker or paste them from the clipboard. Images are saved locally, displayed as thumbnails before sending, and rendered inline in chat messages.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Storage & Schema
- Create `data/uploads/` directory for storing chat image files (gitignored)
- Add `chatAttachments` table to Drizzle schema (id, chatMessageId FK, fileName, filePath, mimeType, sizeBytes, createdAt)
- Add cascade delete from chatMessages to chatAttachments
- Generate and push migration

### Phase 2 — Upload API
- Create `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/upload` route
- Accept multipart form data with image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp)
- Validate file type and size (max 10MB per file)
- Save files to `data/uploads/{projectId}/{nanoid}-{originalName}`
- Return attachment metadata (id, fileName, filePath, mimeType)
- Create `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/uploads/[attachmentId]` to serve images

### Phase 3 — Enhanced MessageInput Component
- Add paste event handler on the textarea to intercept `clipboardData.items` with `type.startsWith('image/')`
- Convert pasted image blobs to File objects and upload immediately
- Add image upload button (paperclip/image icon) next to the send button
- Hidden file input accepting image MIME types, triggered by the button
- Display pending image thumbnails in a preview strip above the textarea
- Allow removing individual thumbnails before sending
- On send, include attachment IDs alongside the message content

### Phase 4 — Message Rendering
- Update MessageList / MarkdownContent to detect and render images associated with messages
- Fetch attachments for each message and display them as inline images below the text
- Support lightbox/modal view on image click for full-size viewing
- Lazy-load images with placeholder skeleton

### Phase 5 — Chat API Integration
- Update `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/messages` to accept an optional `attachmentIds` array
- Link uploaded attachments to the created message
- Update `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/chat/messages` to include attachment metadata in response
- Ensure attachments are cleaned up when messages are deleted (cascade)

epics.title: Spec : option de demander à un agent de mettre à jour la spec, avec champ d'instruction optionnel
epics.description:
Dans la partie **Spec**, ajouter la possibilité de demander à un agent de mettre à jour la spec du projet.

## Comportement attendu

- Un bouton/action dans la vue Spec : **« Mettre à jour la spec avec un agent »**.
- Choix de l'agent via le dropdown global habituel (runtime-only selection, comme sur le reste de l'app).
- **Petit champ d'instruction optionnel** : si l'utilisateur en remplit un, il est injecté dans le prompt pour guider la mise à jour (ex. « mets à jour la section architecture après l'ajout du mode Full Auto »). Si vide, l'agent met à jour la spec à partir de l'état courant du projet (board, releases, code).
- L'agent tourne dans le workspace du projet et **réécrit le fichier spec**.
- Feedback utilisateur : session visible (streaming), puis confirmation de mise à jour de la spec (diff ou message), et affichage de la réponse de l'agent.

## Contraintes

- La spec ne doit pas être modifiée si la session échoue.
- S'aligner sur les patterns existants de lancement d'agent (même mécanisme que tech check / QA).
- Voir aussi le ticket sur la réécriture automatique de la spec (à créer) : cette option manuelle doit coexister proprement avec le mode auto.

user_stories.description: En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux pouvoir demander depuis la vue Spec qu'un agent mette à jour la spec, en choisissant l'agent (dropdown global) et en fournissant éventuellement une instruction.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Done. Committed as `200ec9a`.

## What was built

**UI** — `app/projects/[projectId]/spec/page.tsx` + new `components/spec/SpecUpdateDialog.tsx`
- « Mettre à jour la spec » button (Sparkles, outline) in the Spec header.
- Dialog reuses the shared `AgentDispatchDialog` skeleton: global `NamedAgentSelect` (empty = project default resolved at dispatch), plus an optional instruction `Textarea` with an explicit placeholder. Instruction is sent only when filled.
- After start: status line ("running" with link to the session → "Spec updated by agent." / "failed — spec left unchanged"); the page polls the session every 2s and reloads the spec on success.

**API** — `POST /api/projects/[projectId]/spec/update` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/spec/update/route.ts`)
- Zod-validated `{ instruction?, namedAgentId? }`; 409 `SPEC_UPDATE_PENDING` when a spec update is already queued/running.

**Workflow** — `lib/workflow/spec-update.ts`, modeled on the memory-distill pattern
- Queued `spec_generation` plan-mode session + per-project scheduler closure; agent runs in the project workspace.
- On `answered` completion only, the sanitized output replaces `projects.spec` and `tryExportArjiJson` runs — **a failed/asked/silent session never touches the stored spec** (epic constraint).
- Prompt: `buildSpecUpdatePrompt` in `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts` injects current spec + memory; the user-instruction section appears only when provided and is marked as taking precedence.

## Verification
- New tests: `__tests__/spec-update-dispatch.test.ts` (5 — persistence on success, fence unwrap, failure leaves spec untouched, instruction in prompt only when set, pending guard) and `__tests__/spec-update-dialog.test.tsx` (3 — POST body `{}` when empty, both fields when filled, API error surfaced without a started session).
- Full suite: 302 files / 3393 tests green; `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on changed files.
- Live smoke against `next dev`: created a throwaway project, dispatched → `{sessionId}`, second call 409'd, session prompt contained the instruction, cancel left `spec: null`. Smoke DB removed afterwards.

## Notes for sibling tickets
- The auto spec-rewrite ticket can reuse `dispatchSpecUpdateSession({ projectId, instruction: null, namedAgentId: null })` directly; the 409 guard already serializes manual vs automatic updates.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

The `submit_findings` MCP call is blocked by plan mode, so here is the full report inline.

# Code Review — Spec: option de demander à un agent de mettre à jour la spec

**Scope:** 4 commits on `feature/epic-yoEoq7PH5ad8-…`, 10 files, +1635 lines.
**Verification run:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npx eslint` on all 6 changed source files clean · `npx vitest run` on the 4 new suites → 23/23 passing in 11s.

The architecture is sound and closely mirrors `lib/workflow/memory-distill.ts`: queued session row → per-project scheduler → plan-mode spawn → the agent's entire answer becomes the new spec, persisted **only** on a delivered answer. The "spec unchanged on failure" constraint is correctly implemented and well tested. Four issues block, though.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The module docstrings explain *why* (no `epicId` so the run doesn't occupy an epic's concurrency slot; the 409 rationale; why an unknown named agent rejects instead of falling through) rather than restating the code. Naming is descriptive throughout.

## 2. DRY Principle

### 🟡 Minor — `sanitizeUpdatedSpec` is a byte-identical copy · `lib/workflow/spec-update.ts:97`
Same regex, same body, same docstring as `sanitizeDistilledMemory` (`lib/workflow/memory-distill.ts:353`). A shared helper would carry one test suite and one place to fix its known gaps (a trailing newline after the closing fence, or a language tag with a digit like `md5`, both fall through today).

Wider duplication worth naming: `dispatchSpecUpdateSession` and `dispatchMemoryDistillSession` share ~80 lines of identical scaffolding — logs dir, `cliSessionId`, `createQueuedSession`, and the whole scheduler closure. Two copies is where the shape is confirmed but extraction is still cheap; a third will not be.

### 🟡 Minor — hand-rolled poll loop · `app/projects/[projectId]/spec/page.tsx:85`
`hooks/usePolling.ts` is the codebase's polling idiom, and the session detail page polls **this exact endpoint** with it (`usePolling(loadSession, 3000)`). The self-rescheduling `setTimeout` plus its own `cancelled` flag re-implements it.

## 3. Error Handling

### 🔴 Major — missing `requireGitRepo: true` · `app/api/projects/[projectId]/spec/update/route.ts:38`
`projects.git_repo_path` is nullable (`lib/db/schema.ts:17`) and the dispatcher falls back to `cwd: project.gitRepoPath || process.cwd()` (`spec-update.ts:210`) — Arij's own directory. That fallback is harmless for the memory distill, but **this** prompt instructs the agent to ground the rewrite in "what you find in the repository itself (code, docs, git history)" (`prompt-builder.ts:333`). For a spec-only project the agent reads Arij's source tree, writes a document describing Arij, and it silently replaces the user's spec with `outcome === "answered"`.

The epic asks to align with tech check / QA, and `app/api/projects/[projectId]/qa/check/route.ts:82` does exactly this:
```ts
const found = getProjectOr404(projectId, { requireGitRepo: true });
```
That change also delivers the "erreur lisible avant le démarrage" criterion — the helper already returns a 400 the dialog renders.

### 🔴 Major — one bad poll response reports failure while the run continues · `app/projects/[projectId]/spec/page.tsx:106`
No `res.ok` check. Every non-terminal path collapses to "failed": a network blip or dev-server reload hits `catch` → `setUpdateStatus("failed")` (line 113); a 404 or an HTML 500 page yields `data = {}` → `status === undefined` → falls past the `queued|running` branch to the `else` → `"failed"`. Since `updateStatus === "failed"` is a guard at the top of the effect, polling then stops for good.

The panel renders *"Spec update failed — the saved spec was left unchanged"* with an empty error body — while the agent is still running and will overwrite `projects.spec` minutes later. The user is told the exact opposite of what happens. A Next.js dev-server reload during a multi-minute run triggers this every time.

### 🟡 Minor — `asked_question` becomes a silent dead end · `lib/workflow/spec-update.ts:244`
`success: !!output` makes `markSessionTerminal` write `status: "failed"` alongside `outcome: "asked_question"`, contradicting the documented meaning of the column (`lifecycle.ts:29`, `:350`). The consequence: `createNotificationFromSession` early-returns on `asked_question` (`lib/notifications/create.ts:260`) assuming the workflow posts its own question notification — which this one doesn't. An agent that stops to ask gets a session marked failed, **no notification at all**, and nothing outside the Spec view says a question is waiting.

The `silent` case is a deliberate, documented trade-off and I'd leave it. Also: the suite header at `__tests__/spec-update-dispatch.test.ts:8` claims `asked_question` coverage that doesn't exist — adding it would have surfaced this.

## 4. Performance

### 🔴 Major — unbounded board/changelog in an argv-passed prompt · `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:263`
`buildProjectStateSection` renders every epic, every story and every **full** changelog with no cap, concatenated with the full spec, description and memory — then handed to the CLI as a command-line argument (`args.push("--print", "-p", prompt)`, `lib/claude/spawn.ts:148`). Oversized argv is a failure mode this repo has already hit: the spawn dies with E2BIG before the agent starts, reading as a mysterious instant failure.

Every other embedded block in this file is capped — `slice(0, 500)` (line 730), `MEMORY_DISTILL_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` (2000), `PROJECT_MEMORY_MAX_CHARS`. This one is the odd one out. Recommend per-changelog and per-section caps in the same style, plus a truncation marker so the agent doesn't read a missing epic as "removed from the project" and rewrite the spec accordingly.

### 🟡 Minor — heavy endpoint at a 2s cadence · same file, `:87`
`GET /sessions/[sessionId]` re-reads and re-parses the logs file, re-runs `collectArijActions`, and returns the full session row (including the whole prompt, which embeds the entire spec + board) plus **all three** chunk streams, every tick. Monotonically growing payload for a long run.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. camelCase, PascalCase components, `use*` hooks, `data-testid` kebab-case — all consistent.

## 6. Type Safety

### 🟡 Minor — untyped poll response · `app/projects/[projectId]/spec/page.tsx:92-99`
No `any` annotations (eslint is clean), but `const data = json.data ?? {}` is untyped, so `chunks.map((c) => c.content)` has an implicit-`any` param and the status needs `data.status as string | undefined`. `SessionDetail` already models this response (`sessions/[sessionId]/page.tsx:27`) but isn't exported. Nothing here is checked against the route's real shape, so a field rename degrades silently to a blank stream instead of failing the build.

## 7. Testing

Genuinely good — the dispatch/persistence matrix (answered, fence-unwrapped, silent, spawn failure, stale agent, pending guard, board embedding) and the UI wiring are covered through the real components rather than mocks.

### 🔵 Suggestion — real 2.1s timers · `__tests__/spec-page-update-feedback.test.tsx:68`
`tick()` sleeps on a real timer to outrun the 2s poll; the file takes 8.8s of the 11s total and needs per-test 15000 timeouts. `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` gives the same determinism at zero wall-clock.

**Gap:** the route itself is untested — the 409 `SPEC_UPDATE_PENDING` path and the 400 `SpecUpdateAgentNotFoundError` mapping have no coverage.

## 8. API Design

Envelope, status codes and the `code` field all follow `lib/api/route-helpers.ts`. Correct 400/404/409 usage.

| Sev | Location | Issue |

| 🔴 Major | `spec/page.tsx:64` | **`refreshSpec()` discards unsaved editor edits.** `spec` is the controlled editor value; on success the poll does `setSpec(d.data.spec ?? "")` with no dirty check. The editor stays enabled for the whole multi-minute run with nothing suggesting the text is about to be swapped — and React replaces the value, so there's no undo. The mirror case is as bad: edit during the run, click Save afterwards, and you PATCH stale text over the agent's output. |
| 🟡 Minor | `SpecUpdateDialog.tsx:78` | **Copy describes behaviour that doesn't exist.** "rewrites SPEC.md" — nothing reads or writes `SPEC.md` anywhere; the only other occurrence is a decorative header label. The prompt explicitly *forbids* the agent from emitting anything but the document (`prompt-builder.ts:352`). A user will go looking for the file, or assume the agent has write permission in their workspace. |
| 🟡 Minor | `SpecUpdateDialog.tsx:107` | **No `confirmDisabled={starting}`.** `busy` only swaps the icon; the gate is the separate prop. Both other consumers pass it (`EpicDetail.tsx:636`, `AgentActionsBar.tsx:441`). A double-click fires a redundant POST whose 409 `setError` lands on an already-closed dialog — so the stale message appears the *next* time it opens. After a refresh the button re-enables (it keys off local state) but the server still sees a running session, so the next click returns a bare 409 with no link to the run. Exposing `hasPendingSpecUpdate` as a `GET` on the same path would let the page adopt the in-flight session. |

But `resolveAgentPrompt("spec_generation")` returns whatever the user configured for generate-spec — a prompt demanding a JSON `{spec, epics[]}` envelope — prepended to a prompt whose CRITICAL section demands raw markdown. A dedicated `spec_update` type also makes the pending guard exact and gets these sessions a real label (`AGENT_TYPE_LABELS` has no `spec_generation` entry, so the detail page shows the raw slug). |

The criterion quotes the epic's own French prose rather than specifying copy — worth a deliberate decision either way. |

| **Major** | **4** |
| Minor | 9 |
| Suggestion | 2 |

The four majors are: the missing `requireGitRepo` guard (wrong-workspace rewrite), the false-failure poll (UI contradicts what actually happens to the spec), the unsaved-edit clobber (data loss), and the uncapped prompt section (known E2BIG failure mode). Each is a small, localized fix.

# Code Review — Spec: option de demander à un agent de mettre à jour la spec

**Scope:** 4 commits, 10 files, +1635 lines.

The architecture is sound and closely mirrors `lib/workflow/memory-distill.ts`: queued session row → per-project scheduler → plan-mode spawn → the agent's entire answer becomes the new spec, persisted **only** on a delivered answer. The "spec unchanged on failure" constraint is correctly implemented and genuinely well tested. Four issues block.

## 1. Readability
No issues found. Module docstrings explain *why* (no `epicId` so the run doesn't occupy an epic's concurrency slot; the 409 rationale; why an unknown named agent rejects rather than falling through) instead of restating the code.

## 2. DRY Principle

**🟡 Minor — `sanitizeUpdatedSpec` is byte-identical to `sanitizeDistilledMemory`** · `lib/workflow/spec-update.ts:93` vs `lib/workflow/memory-distill.ts:353`. Same regex, same body, same docstring. Wider: `dispatchSpecUpdateSession` and `dispatchMemoryDistillSession` share ~80 lines of scaffolding (logs dir, `cliSessionId`, `createQueuedSession`, the whole scheduler closure).

**🟡 Minor — hand-rolled poll loop** · `app/projects/[projectId]/spec/page.tsx:85`. `hooks/usePolling.ts` is the codebase idiom, and `sessions/[sessionId]/page.tsx` polls **this exact endpoint** with it.

## 3. Error Handling

**🔴 Major — missing `requireGitRepo: true`** · `app/api/projects/[projectId]/spec/update/route.ts:38`
`gitRepoPath` is `nullish()` at creation and nullable in schema (`lib/db/schema.ts:17`), and the dispatcher falls back to `cwd: project.gitRepoPath || process.cwd()` (`spec-update.ts:210`) — Arij's own directory. Harmless for the memory distill, but **this** prompt tells the agent to ground the rewrite in "what you find in the repository itself". A spec-only project gets a document describing Arij silently written over the user's spec with `outcome === "answered"`. `qa/check`, `git/status`, `sync` and `stories/[storyId]/build` all pass `{ requireGitRepo: true }`; the overload already returns the 400 the dialog renders, which also delivers the "erreur lisible avant le démarrage" criterion.

**🔴 Major — one bad poll response reports failure while the run continues** · `spec/page.tsx:106`
No `res.ok` check. A 404/500 yields `data = {}` → `status === undefined` → falls past the `queued|running` branch into the `else` → `"failed"`; a network blip hits `catch` → same (line 113). Since `updateStatus === "failed"` guards the top of the effect, polling then stops for good. The panel renders *"Spec update failed — the saved spec was left unchanged"* with an empty error body — while the agent is still running and will overwrite `projects.spec` minutes later. A dev-server recompile during a multi-minute run triggers this every time.

**🟡 Minor — `asked_question` becomes a silent dead end** · `spec-update.ts:244`
`success: !!output` makes `markSessionTerminal` write `status: "failed"` alongside `outcome: "asked_question"` (`lifecycle.ts:368`), and `createNotificationFromSession` early-returns on that outcome (`lib/notifications/create.ts:260`) assuming the workflow posts its own question notification — which this one doesn't. Session marked failed, **no notification at all**. The `silent` case is a deliberate documented trade-off and I'd leave it. Note the suite docstring at `__tests__/spec-update-dispatch.test.ts:8` claims `asked_question` coverage the 11 cases don't contain.

## 4. Performance

**🔴 Major — unbounded board/changelog in an argv-passed prompt** · `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:263`
`buildProjectStateSection` renders every epic, story and **full** changelog uncapped, concatenated with the full spec, description and memory, then handed to the CLI as a single command-line argument (`args.push("--print", "-p", prompt)`, `lib/claude/spawn.ts:148`). Linux caps a single argv entry at `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 128 KiB regardless of the 2 MB `ARG_MAX` this box reports, and there is no prompt-size guard anywhere in `spawn.ts` or the providers. Agent-generated changelogs are multi-KB each, so a mature project crosses that line and the spawn dies with E2BIG before the agent starts. Every other embedded block in this file is capped — `slice(0, 500)` (line 730), `PROJECT_MEMORY_MAX_CHARS`, `MEMORY_DISTILL_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS`. Needs per-changelog and per-section caps with a truncation marker, so the agent doesn't read a missing epic as "removed" and rewrite the spec accordingly.

**🟡 Minor — heavy endpoint at 2s cadence** · `spec/page.tsx:87`. `GET /sessions/[sessionId]` re-reads and re-parses the logs file, re-runs `collectArijActions`, and returns the whole session row (including the prompt, which embeds the entire spec + board) plus all three chunk streams, every tick.

## 5. Naming Conventions
No issues found.

## 6. Type Safety

**🟡 Minor — untyped poll response** · `spec/page.tsx:92-99`. No `any` (eslint clean), but `json.data ?? {}` is untyped, so `chunks.map((c) => c.content)` has an implicit-`any` param and status needs a cast. `SessionDetail` already models this response at `sessions/[sessionId]/page.tsx:27` but isn't exported — a field rename degrades to a blank stream instead of failing the build.

## 7. Testing
Genuinely good — the dispatch/persistence matrix (answered, fence-unwrapped, silent, spawn failure, stale agent, pending guard, board embedding) is exercised against the real migrated schema through `createTestDb`, and the UI through real components rather than mocks.

**Gap:** the route is untested — the 409 `SPEC_UPDATE_PENDING` and 400 `SpecUpdateAgentNotFoundError` paths have no coverage. **🔵 Suggestion:** `spec-page-update-feedback.test.tsx` sleeps on real 2.1s timers (8.5s of the suite's 9.4s, needs per-test 15000 timeouts); fake timers give the same determinism at zero wall-clock.

## 8. API Design
Envelope, status codes and the `code` field follow `lib/api/route-helpers.ts`. Correct 400/404/409 usage.

## Additional findings

| Sev | Location | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 Major | `spec/page.tsx:64` | **`refreshSpec()` discards unsaved editor edits.** `spec` is the controlled editor value; on success the poll does `setSpec(d.data.spec ?? "")` with no dirty check. The editor stays enabled for the whole multi-minute run, and React replaces the value — no undo. Mirror case: edit during the run, click Save after, and you PATCH stale text over the agent's output. |
| 🟡 Minor | `SpecUpdateDialog.tsx:78` | **Copy describes behaviour that doesn't exist.** "rewrites SPEC.md" — nothing reads or writes a `SPEC.md`; the only other occurrence is a decorative header pre-existing on `main`. The session runs in `mode: "plan"`, so the agent *cannot* write files — its answer is the document, stored in `projects.spec` and exported to `arji.json` (`lib/sync/export.ts:77`). |
| 🟡 Minor | `SpecUpdateDialog.tsx:107` | **No `confirmDisabled={starting}`.** `busy` only swaps the icon; the gate is the separate prop, passed by both other consumers (`EpicDetail.tsx:636`, `AgentActionsBar.tsx:441`). Also `resetForm()` runs only on success, so Cancel leaves the typed instruction and any stale error behind. |
| 🟡 Minor | `SpecUpdateProgress.tsx:73` | **Raw `<a href>` for an internal route.** Every other session link uses `next/link`. Full reload remounts with `updateSessionId === null` — the run loses its UI. |
| 🟡 Minor | `spec/page.tsx:188` | **No reload recovery.** Panel state is component-local and never rehydrated; after a refresh the button re-enables while the server still sees a running session, so the next click returns a bare 409. Exposing `hasPendingSpecUpdate` as a `GET` on the same path would let the page adopt the in-flight run. |
| 🟡 Minor | `spec-update.ts:41` | **Reusing `spec_generation` couples this to the generate-spec agent's prompt.** `resolveAgentPrompt` returns the user's DB override, so a configured generate-spec prompt demanding a JSON `{spec, epics[]}` envelope gets prepended to a prompt whose CRITICAL section demands raw markdown. Safe *today* only because the builtin is empty and generate-spec creates no `agent_sessions` row (it uses `activityRegistry`), so the pending guard doesn't collide. A dedicated type also gets these sessions a label — the sessions list page's own `AGENT_TYPE_LABELS` (`sessions/page.tsx:77`) has no `spec_generation` entry and renders the raw slug. |
| 🟡 Minor | `spec/page.tsx:176` | **Only French user-facing string in the app**, and it's the entry point to an all-English flow ("Update the specification with an agent", "Update spec", "Spec update running"). Worth a deliberate call. |

**Matched, not introduced:** rendering `logs.result` raw mirrors `sessions/[sessionId]/page.tsx:417`; the escaped fence in the prompt template mirrors the pre-existing line on `main`.

**On acceptance criteria:** all four stories' criteria are met and tested — button, agent dropdown, optional instruction, streamed session, confirmation with the agent response, spec unchanged on failure. "Le fichier spec est bien modifié sur disque" is satisfied via `projects.spec` → `arji.json`, which is Arij's model — precisely what the dialog copy misdescribes.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| **Major** | **4** |
| Minor | 10 |
| Suggestion | 2 |

The four majors: the missing `requireGitRepo` guard (rewrite grounded in the wrong repo), the false-failure poll (UI states the opposite of what happens to the spec), the unsaved-edit clobber (data loss), and the uncapped prompt section (E2BIG, a failure mode this repo has already hit). epics.title: Échec de build silencieux : « Agent error » sans message d'erreur ni notification
epics.description:
## Problème

Sur un deuxième projet, la tentative de build d'un ticket échoue avec uniquement un message **« Agent error »** en tout petit en bas de l'interface. Aucune indication sur la nature de l'erreur n'est affichée, ni dans l'UI ni via une notification.

## Comportement attendu

Quand un build (ou toute session d'agent) échoue :

1. **Notification** : une notification du système de notifications global doit être émise, avec le **message d'erreur complet** (stderr / sortie de l'agent / raison de l'échec), pas seulement un libellé générique.
2. **Visibilité dans l'UI** : l'erreur doit être visible et lisible sur la carte / le ticket — pas un texte minuscule tronqué. Un clic doit permettre de voir le détail complet (par exemple via la modale de notifications ou la vue session).
3. **Traçabilité** : l'erreur complète doit rester consultable après coup (log de session), pas seulement au moment de l'échec.

## Contexte

- Le système de notifications global existe déjà (E-arij-009, done) — il faut le brancher sur les échecs de session/build.
- Un bug proche a déjà été traité : B-arij-108 (« Le badge "Session failed" réapparaît après un retry réussi ») et E-arij-010 (« trop de cas de "(no textual output)" ») — vérifier que la cause n'est pas liée (sortie vide de l'agent → message générique au lieu de l'erreur réelle).
- Piste probable : quand la sortie de l'agent est vide ou que le process meurt sans stderr, l'UI retombe sur le libellé « Agent error » sans surface pour afficher la raison.

## Critères d'acceptation

- Un build qui échoue déclenche une notification contenant le message d'erreur complet (ou, si l'agent n'a produit aucune sortie, un message explicite le disant + où trouver les logs).
- Le message « Agent error » seul, en tout petit, n'est plus le seul signal : le détail est accessible en un clic.
- L'erreur reste consultable après coup dans l'historique de la session.
- Cas vide/no-output couvert explicitement (cf. leçon E-arij-010).

epics.title: Repenser la création et la configuration des agents : UI simplifiée, suppression de la partie providers
epics.description:
## Contexte

L'UI de création et de configuration des agents est actuellement bloatée et confuse : trop de champs, trop de sections, pas de hiérarchie visuelle. Le parcours de création d'un agent demande à l'utilisateur de prendre des décisions qui ne l' concernent pas (notamment sur les providers, alors que c'est la CLI qui gère ça).

## Objectifs

1. **Parcours de création minimal** : créer un agent nommé en quelques champs (nom, CLI/role, modèle si pertinent), avec des defaults intelligents. Tout le reste se configure en option depuis l'écran de configuration.
2. **Écran de configuration clarifié** : sections clairement séparées, progressive disclosure (options avancées repliées par défaut), chaque champ libellé et documenté.
3. **Suppression de la partie providers** : cette section n'apporte rien (les providers sont gérés par les CLIs). À virer de la création ET de la configuration.
4. **Accessible à un nouvel utilisateur** : un utilisateur qui n'a jamais touché Arij doit pouvoir créer et configurer un agent sans documentation.

## Hors périmètre (à confirmer)

- Le runtime de sélection des agents (dropdown global, cf. E-arij-020) : on ne touche pas au comportement d'exécution, seulement à la UI de config.
- La refactor de multi-provider CLI (E-arij-011) côté backend.

## Questions ouvertes

- Conserver un champ « système / persona » optionnel à la création, ou le reporter uniquement en config avancée ?
- Faut-il proposer des templates de agents (build, review, QA…) lors de la première création ?
- Que faire des données providers déjà sauvegardées sur des agents existants : ignore silencieusement ou migration de nettoyage ?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

Plan mode blocked the `submit_findings` MCP call, so here is the full report inline. Findings are ready to file verbatim once I'm out of plan mode.

# Code Review — Epic: Repenser la création et la configuration des agents

**Range reviewed:** `a4d7560..12a837e` (4 commits, 19 files, +936/−762)
**Verification run:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · 61/61 tests pass across the 7 agent-config suites · working tree clean after the run

---

## What works

The four stories are genuinely implemented, and the structural choices are right.

- **Creation flow is actually minimal.** `NamedAgentsTab.tsx:198-243` — two fields, name + CLI, with `claude-code` pre-selected. Model moved to the row editor only.
- **Progressive disclosure is real.** `AgentConfigPanel.tsx:67-86` — collapsed by default, `aria-expanded` wired, advanced content not merely hidden but unmounted (`{advancedOpen && …}`), so the fetch-driven tabs don't run on open.
- **Providers removal is complete on the UI side.** `ProviderDefaultsTab`, `useAgentProviders` and `PROVIDER_TIERS` are all deleted, and nothing outside `__tests__` still imports them. No dead UI code references providers.
- **`Field` is a good abstraction** (`components/agent-config/Field.tsx`) — `label` and `hint` are required props, so "no field without a label and a hint" is enforced by the type system rather than by discipline.
- **Optional `model` is plumbed correctly end to end.** Every provider adapter guards with `if (model)` (`lib/providers/*.ts`), `spawn.ts:150` too, `zai.ts:34` falls back to `glm-4`, `forensic-prompt.ts:78` renders `"(provider default)"`, and `NamedAgentSelect.tsx:98` shows the name only — so no surface renders an empty `name ()`. An empty model degrades to the CLI default with no runtime error.

**No issues found** in: Performance (no N+1, no new fetches; dropping the loading spinner in `RuntimeSettingsTab` is correct since the provider fetch it gated is gone) · Type Safety (no `any`; `model?: string` consistent across schema, lib, hook) · API Design (no route changes; relaxing `createNamedAgentSchema`/`updateNamedAgentSchema` is a correct relaxation, 201/400/409 shapes unchanged) · DRY (extracting `CliSelect` and `Field` removes real duplication).

---

## Findings

### Major

**1. Create/update errors are silently discarded — `NamedAgentsTab.tsx:169` (and `:74`)**
`const { ok } = await createNamedAgent(…)` drops the `error` that `useAgentConfig.ts:205` deliberately returns. `lib/agent-config/named-agents.ts:78` rejects a case-insensitive duplicate with `"name already exists"` → 400 → nothing renders. A first-time user looking at a CLI select labelled **Claude Code** who names their agent "Claude Code" collides with `GLOBAL_DEFAULT_AGENT_NAME`, which `lib/db/index.ts` seeds on every install. Click, nothing happens, no explanation. Story 4's AC is *"sans bloquer"* — this is the block.
*Fix:* keep the `error`, render it under the Add button. Same for `handleSave`.

**2. CLI dropdown no longer shows which CLIs are installed — `NamedAgentsTab.tsx:40`**
The deleted `ProviderDefaultsTab` rendered green/red availability dots via `useProvidersAvailable()`. That indicator is now gone from every agent-config surface, while `CliSelect` lists all 11 providers as equally plausible. CLI is the *only* choice the minimal flow asks for; picking an uninstalled one yields a valid-looking agent that fails at dispatch, far from where the mistake was made. `hooks/useProvidersAvailable.ts:33` still exists and is still used by the chat panel — this is a few lines of reuse, not new infrastructure.

**3. Review-agent source badge removal exposes shared reviewers to in-place edits — `ReviewAgentsTab.tsx:92`**
`listMergedCustomReviewAgents()` (`lib/agent-config/review-agents.ts:36-57`) merges global rows tagged `source: "global"` with project rows, and line 284 renders all of them identically. `updateAgent`/`deleteAgent` (`useAgentConfig.ts:132`, `:150`) post to the **unscoped** `/api/agent-config/review-agents/:id`. So from a project screen a user edits or deletes a reviewer they can't tell is shared, and it changes for every project. The badge was the only signal; `CustomReviewAgent.source` is now dead in the UI layer.
*Fix:* keep the distinction in user language — `Shared across projects` — or disable Save/Delete on inherited rows.

**4. Orphaned provider defaults are honoured but unreachable — `RuntimeSettingsTab.tsx:22`**
The comment says provider defaults "are gone"; only the editor is. `resolveAgent()` (`agent-resolution.ts:79-149`) still reads `agent_provider_defaults` ahead of the seeded default, and nothing in the UI writes or clears that table any more. Anyone who used the old Providers tab keeps a role pinned to e.g. Codex forever, invisibly, with no way to undo it. Explicit picks still win, so it's a config lock, not a crash. Story 3's AC says *"données ignorées proprement"* and the epic's open question #3 asked "ignore or clean up?" — the diff does neither.
*Fix:* pick one explicitly — a hand-written migration clearing the table (**not** `drizzle-kit generate`), or skip rows with null `namedAgentId` in `resolveAgent()`, or surface a "N roles still pinned — reset" row. Either way, correct the comment.

### Minor

**5. Raw enum values still rendered as badges — `AgentPromptsTab.tsx:74`, `ReviewAgentsTab.tsx:269`**
`<Badge>{prompt.source}</Badge>` prints `builtin` / `global` / `project` verbatim. Story 2's AC forbids *"noms de champs bruts"*, and `agent-config-panel-disclosure.test.tsx:126` asserts this only for the core screen with advanced collapsed — so the section story 2 reorganised isn't covered by the assertion meant to protect it.

**6. Stale pointer to the deleted Providers tab — `NightRunDialog.tsx:424`**
`"Agent Configuration → Providers → Max concurrent agents"`. The sibling comment in `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts:33` *was* updated to "→ Runtime" in this epic; this one was missed, so the two now disagree about where the same setting lives.

**7. Dead mock in both new runtime tests — `runtime-settings-max-concurrent.test.tsx:11`, `runtime-settings-segregation-toggle.test.tsx:9`**
`vi.mock("@/hooks/useAgentConfig", …)` — `RuntimeSettingsTab` no longer imports that module. Harmless now, but a stale factory mock returns `undefined` for any dependency legitimately added later, and the failure reads as a component bug.

**8. Select mock nests `<select>` in `<select>` — `agent-config-panel-disclosure.test.tsx:45`**
React logs `<select> cannot contain a nested <select>.` with a full stack on each of the four tests (confirmed in the run output). `agent-config-journey.test.tsx:89-101` already uses a clean fragment-based variant — worth extracting one shared helper so they don't drift.

### Suggestions

**9. `DEFAULT_REVIEW_AGENT_PROMPT` belongs in `lib/agent-config/constants.ts`** (`ReviewAgentsTab.tsx:32`) — same category as `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS`, which `lib/agent-config/prompts.ts:6` reads from there. The prefill itself is a good call for story 4.

**10. Pre-existing: trimmed save leaves the row permanently dirty** (`NamedAgentsTab.tsx:69`) — `dirty` compares raw state, `handleSave` sends `.trim()`. Predates the epic; flagged only because the diff touches both lines, so a reviewer doesn't read it as new.

**11. Toggle missing `aria-controls`, disclosure state not persisted** (`AgentConfigPanel.tsx:67`) — `aria-expanded` without `aria-controls` is an incomplete pattern; `advancedOpen` resets every time the panel is reopened.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 4 |
| Minor | 4 |
| Suggestion | 3 |

The epic's structure is sound and its four stories are implemented, but three of the four Major findings are regressions or gaps measured against this epic's *own* acceptance criteria — silent create failure and the missing CLI-availability signal both undercut "a new user creates an agent without documentation, without getting blocked", and the review-agent badge removal turned a labelled shared record into an unlabelled one that's still editable in place.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**5. Shared review agents are editable in place with no indication — `ReviewAgentsTab.tsx:284`**
`listMergedCustomReviewAgents()` (`review-agents.ts:36-57`) tags global rows `source: "global"`; the removed badge was the only signal. `updateAgent`/`deleteAgent` (`useAgentConfig.ts:138`, `:151`) post to the **unscoped** route. From a project screen a user now edits or deletes a reviewer shared by every project without knowing it. Fix in user language — `Shared across projects` — or disable Save/Delete on inherited rows.

### Minor

**6. `hooks/useProvidersAvailable.ts:33` is now dead production code** — its only non-test importer at `a4d7560` was `ProviderDefaultsTab.tsx`. `app/api/providers/available/route.ts` and all three `app/api/agent-config/providers/**` routes likewise have zero callers. Story 3's AC says *"aucun code UI mort"*. Reviving the hook is also the cheap fix for #4.

**7. Raw enum rendered as a badge — `AgentPromptsTab.tsx:76`** — `{prompt.source}` prints `builtin`/`global`/`project`. `agent-config-panel-disclosure.test.tsx:126` asserts against raw jargon only on the core screen with advanced collapsed, so the section story 2 reorganised isn't covered by the assertion meant to protect it.

**8. Prompt textarea has no label — `AgentPromptsTab.tsx:81`** — a hint was added, but no `<label>`/`htmlFor`, while every other field on these screens went through `Field`.

**9. Stale pointer to the deleted tab — `NightRunDialog.tsx:424`** — "Agent Configuration → Providers → Max concurrent agents". The sibling comment in `scheduler-constants.ts:33` *was* updated to "→ Runtime" in this epic; the two now disagree.

**10. Dead mock in both new runtime tests — `runtime-settings-max-concurrent.test.tsx:11`, `runtime-settings-segregation-toggle.test.tsx:9`** — `RuntimeSettingsTab` no longer imports `useAgentConfig`. Harmless today; a stale factory mock returns `undefined` for any dependency added later, and the failure reads as a component bug.

**11. Select mock nests `<select>` in `<select>` — `agent-config-panel-disclosure.test.tsx:45`** — React logs a full stack on each of the four tests (confirmed in the run). `agent-config-journey.test.tsx:89-101` already has a clean fragment-based variant; extract one shared helper.

### Suggestions

**12.** `DEFAULT_REVIEW_AGENT_PROMPT` (`ReviewAgentsTab.tsx:32`) belongs in `lib/agent-config/constants.ts` beside `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS`. The prefill itself is a good call for story 4.
**13.** `AgentConfigPanel.tsx:49` — `aria-expanded` without `aria-controls` is incomplete, and `advancedOpen` resets on every reopen.
**14.** Pre-existing (`NamedAgentsTab.tsx:69`): `dirty` compares raw state while `handleSave` sends `.trim()`, so a trailing-space save leaves the row permanently dirty. Flagged only because the diff touches both lines.

---

## Two corrections to the earlier comment on this ticket

- It claimed `useProvidersAvailable` is "still used by the chat panel." It isn't — only the definition and test mocks reference it. That makes it dead code (#6), not a live utility.
- It claimed `lib/db/index.ts` seeds a `"Claude Code"` named agent on every install. Nothing seeds it; no migration inserts into `named_agents`. Finding 1 stands on the ordinary duplicate-name path instead, and the missing seed is precisely what gives finding 2 its teeth.

It also framed the provider-defaults problem as orphaned rows alone. The larger half is the deleted role → agent mapping.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 5 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 3 |

The structure is sound and all four stories are implemented. But removing "providers" took two things with it that were not provider concerns — the role → named-agent assignment and the CLI availability indicator — and three of the five Major findings are measured against this epic's own acceptance criteria: a create that fails in silence, a CLI choice made blind, and a shared reviewer that lost its only label while staying editable in place.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**Code Review**

# Code Review — Epic: Repenser la création et la configuration des agents

**Range:** `a4d7560..12a837e` (4 commits, 19 files, +936/−762)
**Verification this session:** `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 · 61/61 tests pass across the 7 agent-config suites · working tree clean

Plan mode blocks every `mcp__arij__*` call — read-only `get_ticket` returned `Cannot call mcp__arij__get_ticket while in plan mode`, so `submit_findings` is unavailable. Findings are staged verbatim at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-elegant-honey.md` for a session that can file them.

---

## What works

- **Creation is genuinely minimal.** `NamedAgentsTab.tsx:198-243` — name + CLI, `claude-code` preselected, model moved to the row editor.
- **Disclosure is real, not CSS.** `AgentConfigPanel.tsx:67` gates on `{advancedOpen && …}`, so the fetch-driven tabs don't mount until expanded.
- **`Field` (`components/agent-config/Field.tsx`) makes `label` and `hint` required props** — story 2's "no unlabelled field" is enforced by the type system rather than by discipline.
- **Optional `model` is plumbed end to end.** `schemas.ts:125` → `named-agents.ts:55-75` → `useAgentConfig.ts:195`, and every consumer guards on falsy: `spawn.ts:150`, `codex.ts:139`, `zai.ts:31-34` (falls back to `glm-4`). `named_agents.model` is `notNull()` and gets `""`, not null — no runtime error. `NamedAgentSelect.tsx:97` renders the name alone, so no surface shows an empty `name ()`.

**No issues found** in *Performance* (no N+1, no new fetches; dropping the loading spinner in `RuntimeSettingsTab` is correct now that the provider fetch it gated is gone), *Type Safety* (no `any`; `model?: string` consistent across schema/lib/hook; tsc clean), or *API Design* (no route changes; relaxing the two named-agent schemas is a correct relaxation, 201/400/409 shapes unchanged).

---

## Findings

### Major

**1. Role → named-agent assignment deleted with no replacement — `AgentConfigPanel.tsx:41`, `RuntimeSettingsTab.tsx:25`**
The removed `ProviderDefaultsTab` held **two** selects per role: a CLI picker (fair to drop) and a *named-agent assignment* — not a provider concern — that was the only writer of `agent_provider_defaults.named_agent_id`. `resolveAgent()` (`agent-resolution.ts:305-370`) still reads that table project → global → builtin, ahead of everything.
*New installs:* an agent created in the new flow can never become a role default. Dispatch falls back to the seeded `"Claude Code"` row (`lib/db/init.ts:148-173`, pinned to `claude-opus-4-6`) unless the user re-picks by hand at each dispatch via `NamedAgentSelect` — and `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:57` holds that in ephemeral React state, so it doesn't survive a reload.
*Existing installs:* whatever the old tab pinned stays pinned forever, invisibly, with no way to clear it. `RuntimeSettingsTab.tsx:25` says the defaults "are gone"; only the editor is. Story 3's AC requires *"données ignorées proprement"* and open question #3 asked ignore-or-migrate — the diff does neither.
*Fix:* either keep a role-assignment control (named agents only, no CLI picker), or a hand-written migration clearing the table plus skipping it in `resolveAgent()`. **Not** `drizzle-kit generate`. Correct the comment either way.

**2. Create and rename failures are silent — `NamedAgentsTab.tsx:169`, `:74`**
`const { ok } = await createNamedAgent(…)` drops the `error` that `useAgentConfig.ts:191-203` deliberately returns. Concretely reachable in the new flow: `lib/db/init.ts:154-173` seeds a named agent called **"Claude Code"** on every startup, and `named-agents.ts:74-80` rejects case-insensitive duplicates → 400. A first-time user looking at a CLI select labelled *Claude Code* names their agent that, clicks **Add agent**, and nothing happens — no message, no explanation. Story 4's AC is *"sans bloquer"*; this is the block. There's also no `try/catch`: a rejected `fetch` leaves `creating` true and the button spinning forever.

**3. CLI availability signal is gone — `NamedAgentsTab.tsx:24`**
The old tab rendered green/red dots from `useProvidersAvailable()`. `CliSelect` now lists all 11 CLIs as equally plausible, and CLI is the *only* choice the minimal flow asks for. Picking an uninstalled one produces a valid-looking agent that fails at dispatch, far from the mistake. `hooks/useProvidersAvailable.ts` and `/api/providers/available` still exist — reuse, not new infrastructure.

**4. Shared review agents are editable in place with no indication — `ReviewAgentsTab.tsx:284`**
`listMergedCustomReviewAgents()` (`review-agents.ts:36-56`) tags global rows `source: "global"`; the badge this epic removed was the only signal, and global + project rows now render identically. `updateAgent`/`deleteAgent` (`useAgentConfig.ts:132`, `:146`) hit the **unscoped** `app/api/agent-config/review-agents/[agentId]/route.ts`, which does no scope check. From one project a user silently edits or deletes a reviewer every project shares. `CustomReviewAgent.source` is now unused in the UI.

### Minor

**5. `hooks/useProvidersAvailable.ts:33` is now dead production code** — zero non-test importers; its only one at `a4d7560` was `ProviderDefaultsTab`. `app/api/providers/available/route.ts` and all four `agent-config/providers/**` routes likewise have zero clients. Story 3's AC: *"aucun code UI mort"*.

**6. Raw enum rendered as a badge — `AgentPromptsTab.tsx:76`** — `{prompt.source}` prints `builtin`/`global`/`project`. The guard test (`agent-config-panel-disclosure.test.tsx:118`) only asserts against jargon on the core screen with advanced collapsed, so the section story 2 reorganised isn't covered by the assertion meant to protect it.

**7. Prompt textarea has no label — `AgentPromptsTab.tsx:81`** — this epic added a hint below it but no `<label htmlFor>`, while every other control on these screens went through `Field`.

**8. "provider" still shown to users — `StatsTab.tsx:121`** — "Runs per named agent and provider". The epic renamed provider → CLI in `RuntimeSettingsTab.tsx:205`; the same screen now speaks two vocabularies.

**9. Stale pointer to the deleted tab — `NightRunDialog.tsx:424`** — "Agent Configuration → Providers → Max concurrent agents". The sibling comment at `scheduler-constants.ts:32` *was* updated to "→ Runtime" in this epic; the two now disagree.

**10. Dead mock in both new runtime tests — `runtime-settings-max-concurrent.test.tsx:11`, `runtime-settings-segregation-toggle.test.tsx:9`** — `RuntimeSettingsTab` no longer imports `useAgentConfig`. Harmless today; a stale factory mock returns `undefined` for any dependency added later, and the failure reads as a component bug.

- Comment 1 said `useProvidersAvailable` is "still used by the chat panel". It isn't — zero non-test importers (finding 5).
- Comment 2 said "nothing seeds that name; no migration inserts into `named_agents`". The seed isn't a migration: it's `seedDefaultNamedAgent()` at `lib/db/init.ts:148`, run by `initDb()` on every connection open. Roles therefore still resolve to a working agent, so finding 1 is a config-reachability regression rather than a dead resolution chain — and that same seeded `"Claude Code"` row is exactly what makes finding 2 reachable on a fresh install.

epics.title: Kanban Workflow Stability & Real-Time Synchronization
epics.description:
Comprehensive refactor of the ticket workflow system to eliminate erratic behaviors, ensure consistent state transitions, and provide real-time updates without page refresh. This epic addresses critical bugs where tickets move to 'Done' prematurely or don't respect review workflows, while adding WebSocket-based live synchronization and enhanced visual feedback through animations.

Implementation Plan:
1. Workflow Rule Engine: Implement strict state machine for ticket transitions with explicit guards (e.g., no 'Done' without completed review, no premature closure when agent asks questions)
2. WebSocket Infrastructure: Set up Socket.io or native WebSocket server for bidirectional communication, broadcasting ticket updates, agent session status, and column movements to all connected clients
3. Event-Driven Architecture: Unify agent hooks (build complete, review complete) and manual user actions under consistent event bus that enforces workflow rules
4. Animation System: Enhance dnd-kit with custom transitions for programmatic moves (agent-triggered) and add visual indicators (sounds optional, glow effects) for state changes
5. Optimistic UI Updates: Implement optimistic updates with rollback capability for instant feedback, confirmed by WebSocket events
6. Agent Session Integration: Ensure agent session lifecycle (start, resume, completion) properly gates ticket transitions and broadcasts status in real-time

epics.title: Repasse complète des transitions automatiques de tickets : états orphelins, full auto et promotion review
epics.description:
## Contexte

Les transitions automatiques de tickets (full auto, pipeline, handlers de fin de session) sont erratiques. Trois symptômes signalés :

1. **Full auto — ticket aspiré du backlog mais jamais passé en `in_progress`** : le superviseur prend un ticket en backlog, un agent démarre dessus, mais le statut ne bouge pas → ticket bloqué dans un état incohérent (agent actif + colonne non buildable), et n'arrive jamais en review. ⚠️ Hypothèse à vérifier d'entrée : la spec E-arij-097 prévoit de builder `todo` + `in_progress` sans agent, **pas** le backlog. Si le sweep pioche quand même dans le backlog, soit c'est un écart à la spec (restreindre l'éligibilité), soit il faut ajouter la transition `backlog → in_progress` au driver — à trancher.
2. **B-arij-104** : dev fini mais ticket jamais passé en `review` (signalé alors qu'une session build tournait encore dessus, 21/08 08:05 UTC). À investiguer : outcome terminal nul ou « answered » sans promotion, promotion en scope story qui exige toutes les sœurs en review/done alors que les stories sont à 0/4, re-pickup infini par le sweep auto.
3. **Transitions globalement erratiques** : le code qui fait avancer les tickets est réparti entre `lib/auto-mode/` (engine + select + merge), `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` (driver), les routes build/review, les handlers d'outcome terminal et le moteur `lib/workflow/engine.ts` — sans vue d'ensemble ni garantie d'invariant.

## Références

- **E-arij-097** (done) — design du full auto : sélecteurs, pièges connus (re-review infinie, question d'agent, merge non approuvé, budgets), contrat « le driver déplace les tickets, le superviseur ne fait que dispatcher ».
- **B-arij-104** — symptôme vivant (build → review non branché / non régulier).
- Moteur de workflow : `lib/workflow/engine.ts` (gardes), `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts` (`applyTransition` + event + log).

## Questions ouvertes

- Full auto : éligibilité au départ = `todo` uniquement (conforme E-arij-097) ou `backlog` aussi avec transition préalable vers `in_progress` ?
- Epic multi-stories : promotion en `review` seulement quand TOUTES les stories sont review/done, ou dès que l'effort epic-level est fini ? Si la première, l'UI doit expliquer le blocage (ex. badge « stories 0/4 »).
- Un ticket rejeté en review qui retombe en `in_progress` : le full auto le reprend automatiquement (c'est le comportement spec) — on le garde ?
- Une transition refusée par le moteur (garde) doit-elle notifier l'utilisateur, ou juste log ?

## Contrainte

Le fix ne doit pas casser les exclusions existantes du full auto (tickets occupés, `isAwaitingReply`, parkés, re-review fraîcheur cf. pièges E-arij-097). Risque de chevauchement de code avec B-arij-104 (sessions/transition) — coordonner.

user_stories.title: Inventaire et carte des transitions automatiques
user_stories.description: Cartographier chaque chemin de code qui change le statut d'un ticket : sweep auto mode (select + merge), driver pipeline (lancement build → in_progress, build ok → review, review négative → in_progress), routes build/review, handlers d'outcome terminal (success/answered/error/asked_question), merge auto. Vérifier que tout passe par `applyTransition` avec les gardes du moteur (aucun bypass d'écriture directe sur le statut), documenter la machine à états résultante (transitions + raisons) en commentaire dans le code ou dans la spec, et lister les incohérences trouvées dans le ticket.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Liste exhaustive des sites d'appel d'`applyTransition` (ou d'écriture de statut hors moteur) avec fichier:ligne
- [ ] Toute écriture de statut passe par le moteur de workflow avec une raison loggable
- [ ] Machine à états documentée (état source → état cible, déclencheur, source)
- [ ] Les anomalies trouvées (bypass, double dispatch, transition manquante) sont listées dans un commentaire du ticket

user_stories.title: Règle « pas d'état orphelin » : un ticket avec session active est toujours en in_progress
user_stories.description: Définir et forcer l'invariant : une session build active (queued/running) sur un ticket ⇒ statut `in_progress`, quel que soit le point de départ (backlog/todo). Traiter le symptôme full auto signalé : si le sweep est éligible sur le backlog, la transition vers `in_progress` doit précéder ou accompagner le dispatch — sinon restreindre l'éligibilité au todo (trancher la question ouverte). Une transition en échec (garde du moteur) doit être loggée avec le ticket et le motif, jamais avalée silencieusement, et ne doit pas laisser le ticket dans un état intermédiaire.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Après un dispatch build (full auto, pipeline ou manuel), le ticket est en `in_progress` dans la même passe (aucune fenêtre d'état orphelin visible sur le board)
- [ ] Éligibilité de départ du full auto tranchée et implémentée (todo seul OU backlog avec transition préalable), consignée dans le ticket
- [ ] Tout échec de transition produit une entrée de log identifiable (ticket + motif) et n'est pas silencieux
- [ ] Test unitaire : dispatch depuis backlog et depuis todo aboutit aux deux cas à `in_progress`

user_stories.title: Régulariser la promotion build → review (cas B-arij-104)
user_stories.description: Reproduire et corriger le cas où une session build se termine (dev fini) sans que le ticket passe en `review`. Points à investiguer : outcome terminal nul ou `answered` non traité comme fin de build, promotion en scope story conditionnée par le statut de toutes les stories sœurs (épic à 0/4 stories qui ne montera jamais), re-pickup par le sweep auto avant que la promotion ait eu lieu, verrou/mutex de sweep qui laisse tomber la transition. À l'issue, une build terminée avec succès doit aboutir de façon déterministe à `review` (epic scope) ou rester en `in_progress` avec une raison explicite loggée (ex. stories restantes), jamais stagner sans explication.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Le scénario B-arij-104 est reproduit (test ou reprod commentée) et la cause racine documentée
- [ ] Build ok + toutes stories review/done ⇒ `review` ; sinon `in_progress` avec raison explicite (ex. « 2 stories restantes ») visible dans l'activity log
- [ ] Pas de re-dispatch du sweep sur un ticket dont la session vient de se terminer sans que la promotion ait été tentée
- [ ] Tests de couverture des branches d'outcome (success / answered / error / asked_question)

user_stories.title: Suite de tests de régression sur les invariants de la machine à états
user_stories.description: Mettre en place une suite de tests automatisés couvrant les chemins dorés et les pièges connus du full auto (cf. E-arij-097) : backlog/todo → in_progress (build lancé), in_progress → review (build ok, stories complètes), review → done (review approuvée, garde a completed review + pas de commentaires ouverts), review → in_progress (rejet, sans agent dessus), idempotence du sweep (un ticket occupé/attendu n'est jamais re-dispatché), exclusion des tickets en `asked_question` (isAwaitingReply), et merge refusé tant que la review n'est pas propre. La suite doit tourner en CI et échouer si un invariant est violé.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Un test par invariant listé ci-dessus, tous au vert
- [ ] Le test d'idempotence du sweep prouve qu'aucun double dispatch n'est possible sur une même passe et la passe suivante
- [ ] La suite est branchée sur le pipeline CI existant
- [ ] Documentation de la suite dans la spec (quel invariant quel test)
